Do not recommend this game. Go on the DD2 forums and read the "Game Feedback" subforum for a good idea of all the things that are wrong with this game. I used to LOVE DD1 and I'm still playing DD2 because it genuinely is fun but I hate myself for it because Trendy truly just don't deserve anyone's support at this point.
There are countless easily fixable bugs which have existed for who knows how long and keep getting ignored because the devs are too busy creating the next moneygrab event or whatever. Bugs you come across every single time you play. They're not critical but they can be extremely annoying, especially considering the fact that they could all probably be fixed in a single day by a competent programmer. The heroes are grossly unbalanced and a lot of towers are completely useless.
Inventory space is extremely limited, events and game mechanics(eggs, lockboxes etc) add a LOT of useless clutter items while extra inventory space costs money. The endgame content requires several builder heroes, so many in fact that you have to buy extra character slots just to have everything you need. Many aspects of the game such as item upgrading or spinning this ridiculous event wheel have unnecessary animations you have to sit through and although the upgrade wheel does have a skip function it's really buggy and only seems to work about half the time.
Item stats are horrible, there is no leeway or room for customization. There is a certain type of item you want for a certain type of hero and there is no alternative. You get that perfect roll or it's trash.
This game has potential to be amazing, the concept is a lot of fun and the artwork in this game is just awe inspiring. Really one of the best looking games I've ever seen. However it's being ruined by the devs seemingly focusing purely on things that can make them money and turning a blind eye to things that will make the gaming experience better for the players. I personally will not spend a cent on this game until Trendy makes a LOT of changes and I will tell anyone who asks to stay away from the game because even if it is a lot of fun right now it's not worth all the frustration caused by bugs and dumb gameplay design decisions.
In case anyone's still on the edge about this game, let me illustrate the kind of crap you can expect: There is a gamemode named Onslaught. It is quite hard, possibly the hardest game mode. In Onslaught you can decide what kind of loot you want - weapons, armor, trinkets, pets or gold. Now any reasonable person would expect the gold farming mode to be the most efficient gold farm in the game right? When there is a dedicated gold farming mode you expect that to be a good way to go about farming gold.
Well, you'd be disappointed because it's completely useless. You could faceroll a regular campaign map on Easy difficulty and earn more gold than doing the Onslaught gold farm on Nightmare.
This is the kind of crap Trendy's playerbase has to put up with. It's not a huge problem in itself, it just illustrates very clearly how misguided the developers are. They add things which make no sense, ignore things that should have been fixed months ago and generally just mess up everything.

However, you are an investigative journalist, and not some gun and sword toting combat expert so it does make sense.
The game mainly consists of taking in the creepy visuals as you try to unravel the mystery of just what is going on. The art and scenes of grusome horror are properly unsettling. The voice acting for the games few characters is solid and the pacing is well done, so while there are the times when you must sneak past, around, or hide from enemies there are large portions that are just tension building nightmares.
Red Barrels has managed to cram in a lot of attention to detail, right down to the scared breathing when you are being hunted.

normally don't do these but i only played this game for a little bit and im already loving it so thought it was worth a review. considering this game is still early access and its already so good i couldnt imagine what this game will have to offer in the future. the graphics are awesome. if you can run this game at highest settings its just very stunning. theres allot of survival simulator games out there but the long dark is by far one of the best. its realistic details and futures are very nice. it has a few difficulty modes and the normal one alone is really challenging. i love how one of the modes allows you to just explore without having to worry about anything. this is great if you just wanna learn the maps or see the environments. this game is really great in the fact that it focuses on mother nature being the threat to you. Any survival expert will tell you mother nature is the hardest thing to face in a survival situation.  again i cant wait to see what this game will have to offer in the future. below i will list my pros and cons that i can think of from the top of my head.
pros:
- graphics are amazing
- games engine/system feels good when playing.
- environments are realistic.
- challenging. you really feel like your trying to survive.
- no stupid humans/zombies/monsters/mutants trying to kill you. just mother nature and her power.
- realistic human needs in a survival situation.
- details. the developers did a really good job at the small details in the game. every good gamer knows the little details in the game are what makes it good. i love the fact i can find a small cabin and explore in it finding a fridge in a kitchen with cans of fruit or soda, closets/drawers with clothes, bathrooms with aid supplies. the buildings/homes/shelters/cabins ect. are just done really well.
cons:
- early access. this technically cant really count as a con, but if you have already done all the maps and explored everything, it does get boring. currently the game doesnt have allot to offer, meaning more maps and items/objects in game, so im hoping for more in the future.
- if you have a bad start at a beginning of a game, your pretty much screwed. but this counts as a sorta fun aspect of the game of how easily rekt you can get.
at $20 for this game id say that as of right now for early access its tuff to say if its worth it. if you get this game on a sale price like i did then definitly go for it.
only things im wishing the developers will add to the game are more maps, environments to explore, more challenges, more objects/items, and i know this is ment to be a single player game, but i wish they could add a co-op option in this game. i know allot of people will disagree or how un likely this will happen, but it would be fun to try to survive with a buddy. it would only add more challenges to keep both people alive. and im sure allot more people will buy this game if it had a co-op option.

The Howler is a short indie hot air balloon simulator developed by Antanas Marcelionis and released in mid 2014.
There is a progressive story about the “Viceroy of Vilnius, Antanas Sidabras”, that is told through the 15 levels of the game.
Aesthetically speaking, the game has some really visually interesting graphics; the art is hand drawn and the “architecture actually exists in Vilnius today”, according to Antanas Marcelionis.
There are two control choices: the volume of your voice
, when the microphone picks up your voice being loud enough, your hot air balloon goes up.
Alternatively, simply use a keyboard, pressing space to go up, and then any other key drops your cargo (including your Steam screenshot button, so beware the screenshot!)
You need to dodge objects that may pop your balloon, and move into air currents that will push you to the right or left. While the game is very straightforward and controls very easily, it's definitely not an “easy” game.
There are no steam achievements for The Howler, quite frankly there isn't enough game to give very many achievements. If achievements were added at some point, it would be along the lines of “beat the game”, “find the hidden level codes”, and anything else would be along the lines of "high score".
The Howler is priced at $4.99, I spent only 1.5 hours to beat the game. By my value system
, this game is a bit too high priced. However, when on sale it's a fair price.
In the end, the developers are indie so the prices tend to be lower and go on sale often, you could argue for buying the game just to support the developers.

The Howler is simple: there is only one button to control: Click to make the balloon go up, do NOT click to make it drop. Different wind layers (of different strengths) means you will move left or right depending on the altitude. You move the balloon from launch pad to destination pad. As you work your way through the over a dozen missions (and there's a bit of a plot) you get complications, like more wind layers, requirement to pick up one or more cargo packs at an intermediate platform, and later, airborne obstacles that gets in your way. A light touch of your balloon against something is okay, heavier touch and your balloon goes POOF.
The difficulty curve feels rather uneven. There's a mission at about halfway where you need to land the balloon, with 2 cargo boxes loaded, THROUGH the mouth of a statue (going at a diagonal). Somehow the balloon felt much more delicate. I made it once without the cargo, but can not make it with the cargo after over a dozen attempts.
Still, as a simple and cheap game it does provide an interesting challenge.

First of all I love the idea and concept around this and all the RPG makers, but they all do have a lot of downfalls.  I love being able to make custom weapons, armor, abilities, encounters, characters, maps, etc, and etc.  Let's be honest though, if you just use the base maker to publish a game, it's not sellable or at least highly disregarded, if not completely.
You need to add your own art (which is very self-rewarding), add your own sprites (for unique character and monster development that works with the art added), custom music a plus (not necessarily a game changer) and at least mild scripting.
Usually you can find the proper scripts and/or coding for various ideas you might have (like forums or You Tube), but sometimes it's not available and you have to figure it out alone.  You can ask around, but even that can be very taxing, given how toxic the community can be.  You have to add things to increase the uniqueness of your adventure.  Want to make this multiplayer? (Local is easier than online)  Good Luck: P
All-in-all this is not a hands free maker that from basic use will result in sought after public sales.  Let us be honest and state the truth is that although there is a ton of free knowledge out there to help you; that you need to do a lot of legwork outside of the basic maker.  Also, what is easier for someone else you might find very difficult for yourself until you have practiced things a few times (most scripts and code are copy and paste, but not always).  They won't advertise it this way, because it would not sell as well; as a needs more work from you advertisement.  So if you are new and want the rpg maker among rpg makers that is stand alone and ready to publish and that you can actually sell.....The answer is none of them are best sellers by themselves and all need some work outside of what the basic maker can provide.
Do I recommend this?   YES!
Do you need to learn things outside of the maker(s)?   YES!
Can you make a game with trying all this extra work within 100 hours?  YES, but the more time and effort = greater outcome
Is it fun to create a game without marketing?   YES!
Are all makers created equally?   YES!  and  NO!
---they are all capable of adding outside additions (art, sprites, scripts, etc and etc), but how they ---handle those new additions is what makes the newer ones superior.
Rating:  7.5/10.0
If they added the basic-most sought after scripts/coding like side battle, multiplayer and many others into the game = 9.0/10.0

In this air current and physics based game you will have to navigate safely through level upon level completing tasks while on the clock. In this 2D game you will spend most of your time in a hot air balloon where you will have to master the different speeds of the air currents while taking into consideration that air can blow in both directions.
Graphically The Howler definitely has that aged look to it. I don't mean that it looks dated it just looks more like a steam-punk Victorian age type of feel. One of the things I like about the art style in this game is that it gives you the look of a city or area of the city while not overly cluttering up the screen.
This game is basically played with just a couple of buttons and/or your voice. I know that sounds a bit crazy, but if you have a good enough mic you can issues increases and decreases in altitude by the level of your voice. Do you want to go higher, get louder, you want to descend, well just get quieter. I wouldn't recommend being silent that might cause a not so fun crash, but hey you never know until you try it.
One of the things that really impressed me with The Howler was the fact that if you had the tutorial text on you could easily pick up this game and be able to play it. Now I know that there are games that put you through the tutorial once and then disable, but in this game it doesn't and that's not a problem. Instead of constantly taking the player out of the game by throwing up dialogue boxes that you have to click ok or next on they put the text into the background of the game and once you start moving around it just vanishes.
Now there is a slight downside to this game and that is it DEFINITELY feels like a port of a tablet or phone game. The resolution for the game can't be changed so you'll be faced with playing in a small box on your screen. The other thing is that as easy as the controls are for some reason the mouse button just doesn't seem to translate as well as say a tap and hold on a touchscreen, maybe that's just me, but I think it makes a difference.
So if you are looking for a challenging puzzle game to play with some interesting yet simple controls you are going to want to pick up this game. I'm not going to lie there are definitely some of the levels where it took me more tries than it should have, but that sense of accomplishment when you do gain enough speed to negate the wind going the opposite direction, or the precision flying/floating required to navigate treacherous locations is pretty astounding. So with that I'm giving this game a 7.5 out of 10.

Today I will be reviewing a video game called Red Orchestra 2. The game was developed by Treyarch (The same people responsible for such classics as : The Great Gatsby, A Clockwork Orange and Super Mario Brothers) and published by Ubisoft.
Let's talk a bit about the game :
The game takes place in a post apocalyptic Paris in the year 2250. When the game begins, you can see society rebuilding itself all around you. Society has been split into 2 sides : The neo-nazis and the capitalists. The neo-nazis are a group led by Adolf Hitler's brain which was recovered by the Illuminati from the very same bunker where Hitler commited suicide. The second group is led by Rndrew Ayan. He is a curious Lovecraft inspired repairman, whose seeking to bring Paris back to it's former glory through any means necessary. The game offers you two ways to play, join the nazis in their quest to take over Paris for the Führer or join the capitalists to restore things to the way they were. The story is amazing. One minute I found myself laughing at the obscure situations that the capitalist soldiers found themselves in, the next I was crying when they lost the Eiffel tower because Sgt. Johnson (Who is a key character in the Capitalist campaign) wanted to send a telegram to his wife back in Austria who was missing him dearly.
Let's talk about the game's mechanics next :
The game is presented in a 2D Bird's Eye perspective, at first I thought this was odd, however it becomes apparent that this was the directors vision and the game is perfect as is. One of they key mechanics of the game is the point'n'click-esque interface, featuring options such as : "Insult", "Batter", "Shoot" and "Heil". Characters in the game react to your every move, from simply moving around to doing key story changing events such as demolishing the Eiffel tower ( which is entirely optional ). The game blends the 2D, Run and gun, Romance, Adventure and Puzzle game elements within it seamlessly to create a unique experience the likes of which will probably never be bested.
Move over Call of Duty Ghosts, Medal of Honor Warfighter and Battlefield 4. There's a new king in town and his name is Red Orchestra 2.

I'm going to start by saying I have never played the Tales series before; this was my first taste of it. Perhaps I am lacking the apperciation for the series that other longtime players have, so if you're starting with this game perhaps this review will be more useful to you.
When this game first came out I was really excited to get it. It was super amazing on the outside and I couldn't wait for it to go on sale so I could buy it. However upon purchase and play I have to admit I was disappointed. I would never reccoment buying at full price, and even at 20$ I felt that it wasn't really worth it. Most of the game is cutscenes, which kind of makes me feel like I'm watching a movie instead of playing a game. I stopped playing before I finished the game and I don't feel any worse for it.
While I appreciated not having to grind for levels the only real gameplay were the battles- and lots of them. It took alot of time to run from place to place, and the battles were automatically structured which left no room for creative interprentation. I essentially spam clicked my mouse for the entire game- which sure damaged my wrists after awhile-and then sat back and watched really long cutscenes. The game doesn't require you to do any thinking of your own and the only difficult boss battle I had to face could only be fought by turning off the 'auto battle feature', which is difficult to find unless you go looking for it. I've never even had to use a healing item.  My playthrough was in normal mode,  so I can't imagine what easy might be like.
While the story was good, as a newcomer to the series I felt like there was still gaps in the story where only a previous history of the games could complete the picture. There were concepts that weren't fully explained and it felt like some of the rules you were expected to already know.
As somone who has played all kinds of RPGS, I can say that Tales of Zestria had a highly structured story and did not leave any kind of room for the player to grow or explore. It's the kind of spoonfeeding expected in elementary school, and without any kind of real challange the video game is just incomplete. If you're into alternate fantasy worlds then this game can absolutely stroke that feel, but unless the game is on sale for cheap, it's not worth the money. Put it towards a more exciting game.

Banished is the most cathartic game I've ever played. During a particularly stressful time in my life this little gem popped up in the steam summer sale and has received most of my attention since.
In this game, you play an omnipotent and omnipresent overlord of a small and yearning-to-thrive midevil hamlet. Starting with a handful of people and a place to store goods, this simcity-like simulator encourages you to build your little hamlet from nothing into a bustling town. In the process, you need to manage your people's heath, happiness, hunger and warmth.
Banished is a very calming exercise. You have no invading hordes to worry about, no political alliances to manage and no trade routes to maintain. This is city management at its purest form. Like SimCity, you may have some disasters.. a sickness here, loss of crops there.. but these "disasters" are few and far between and often easily managed. (Though, admitted, I did have one early game in which a tornado decided to just roll right through my town killing all but 6 of my people.)
The goal here is to build. With building comes additional management. Placement becomes key. Pathing becomes a puzzle. Your little dominion grows into a bustling small town. Your blacksmiths tink tink tink the days away. The chatter of your folk is omnipresent. The harridness of the small town grows into a bustling small city.
This is your world. You created it.
Cathartic.
(Notes: The game has infinite replayability, like any city sim.. however it does support Steam Workshop and there's a lot of great stuff on there.)

Blood and Bacon is a indie game that is unique to say the least. It may not be the most AAA title from popular developers, but that does not make this game just as good. Not only did this game meet my standards but also exceeded. This game when above and beyond the Call of Duty (which this game is nothing like).
Story- well to say the least of the story, there is one that i haven't exactly found out. This games story makes you really dig deep into the game, as they did not just do cut scenes and put the story out in the open. I personally like this approach to the game, as this makes the game more deep then you would think on first hand when playing the game.
Game play-The single player was fun to play through without cheats, although cheats are a totally viable option (if you want every day to be revenge day). I couldn't test the multi player as i didn't have any friends who play this game. However- they put in a whole alpha phase to the multi player (meaning it is currently being tested) and they put in a harder game mode for the multi player if you want to, along with server commands. If you have friends, play it with them, it will only make the game more enjoyable. Single player is just as fun however, so either way you can not go wrong. The weapons in the game are just as good as you would expect them to be in other shooters. They are balanced, fun and easy to use, and not one gun is better then the other, so its all based on how you want to play. Although the number of guns you get are small, this is a good thing, so you are not over whelmed with what to pick and choose. Hit boxes are up to standards with other games.  This game also has gore to it, as the title suggests, meaning body parts go flying if the enemy is shot the right way. You can also kick them and complete an achievement with them.
Sound-The sound in this game is very well made. This isn't a shooter that is supposed to be realistic, so don't go judging the game on that end. Instead, judge it on how clear the sound is. The sound is very clear  to say the least. There is also no sound delay, so you wont feel like the sound is lagging (this can be very frustrating)
Graphics-Although the graphics are not like Destiny or Fall Out 4 on the PC, this game is not supposed to be like that. The graphics were made to please the eye, while also being not so strong that you cant play it on non gaming or old PCs, or even a laptop. I got 60 Frames Per Second (FPS) while played this game every time I did. I never Experienced any lag except if I had a browser open while playing, but this is because my laptop is not the most graphically enhanced. This game is about the experience, and not the power about it (even an achievement for turning up the "graphics" lol).
Over all rating-If you like shooter games, this does not fall below even the most modern shooters. This game visually gives me a vibe of Retro games like Left 4 Dead, while still giving me a sensation that describes the most modern games.
This game could have easily been priced up to 30 dollars for how good it is, but the developers decided to put the game to just a dollar, to make a profit off of the game but still be affordable so everyone could play the game.
Rating 10/10. Recommended for people who like: Shooters, arcade games, multi player games, and value games.

tl;dr: Fun ship building, fighting and base capturing. No idea why people are crapping on this game. 7/10.
Not sure why this game is getting so much hate. I can see some balancing issues, but nothing that can't be fixed with the right ship design. I have a couple different designs that are really fun to play with and it took a long while to get here. A lot of the first ships you build are going to be crappy. If you focus only on looks, you leave yourself at a huge disadvantage. It's a good practice to make sure that every block is touching at least two others, then armor up any joints or critical areas like your core. You're probably going to have to try and copy other people's designs and replay battles in your mind to figure out what your weak spots are and then constantly improve your designs. Thankfully, you unlock more free structure blocks and extra points to add stuff to your ship at every level up, so there is almost always something on your to do list to make your ship better.
As for tactics, if you keep getting stomped, try going with a faster ship like a frigate and tackle enemies through dodging and score points by rushing to capture points. Or if that isn't your play style, go for armor, shields and range with a destroyer or battleship class and focus on defense. If you drop your ship down to 2 engines, then you can put a lot more armor on your ship and add a hyperspace jumper to get to your points faster. The tactical possibilities are endless.
I've put in 30+ hours into the game and it's fun. I really enjoy the ship building and can see putting in more time. Right now the community is taking a poop on the game and I'm not sure why. It's fun, balanced enough, and free. It reminds me of what Robocraft used to be until they patched it over 9000 times. I think if people stop fanboy raging and do what they're supposed to do with games (play and enjoy them) then they'll see that this game is pretty fun and worth a couple quick matches while enjoying a beer every other night.
I'm having fun and even though there are a lot of things to make your ship unique, I hope they come out with some more texture packs and upgrades or maybe another weapon type. Also there are only 3 maps in the main battle mode. I hope they add at least one or two more. In that sense the game is a bit limited, but like all multiplayer games, if the players aren't there then there might not be much more content coming. Another side effect is that matchmaking takes around a minute, but can go up to two minutes to find a match. Considering each match is 5v5, it shouldn't be that hard to find 9 other people, but it seems like it is.
I hope people pull the sticks out of their asses and get on and enjoy this game. More people in matchmaking always a good thing. I definitely recommend this game. 7/10.

Today I will be reviewing a video game called Red Orchestra 2. The game was developed by Treyarch (The same people responsible for such classics as : The Great Gatsby, A Clockwork Orange and Super Mario Brothers) and published by Ubisoft.
Let's talk a bit about the game :
The game takes place in a post apocalyptic Paris in the year 2250. When the game begins, you can see society rebuilding itself all around you. Society has been split into 2 sides : The neo-nazis and the capitalists. The neo-nazis are a group led by Adolf Hitler's brain which was recovered by the Illuminati from the very same bunker where Hitler commited suicide. The second group is led by Rndrew Ayan. He is a curious Lovecraft inspired repairman, whose seeking to bring Paris back to it's former glory through any means necessary. The game offers you two ways to play, join the nazis in their quest to take over Paris for the Führer or join the capitalists to restore things to the way they were. The story is amazing. One minute I found myself laughing at the obscure situations that the capitalist soldiers found themselves in, the next I was crying when they lost the Eiffel tower because Sgt. Johnson (Who is a key character in the Capitalist campaign) wanted to send a telegram to his wife back in Austria who was missing him dearly.
Let's talk about the game's mechanics next :
The game is presented in a 2D Bird's Eye perspective, at first I thought this was odd, however it becomes apparent that this was the directors vision and the game is perfect as is. One of they key mechanics of the game is the point'n'click-esque interface, featuring options such as : "Insult", "Batter", "Shoot" and "Heil". Characters in the game react to your every move, from simply moving around to doing key story changing events such as demolishing the Eiffel tower ( which is entirely optional ). The game blends the 2D, Run and gun, Romance, Adventure and Puzzle game elements within it seamlessly to create a unique experience the likes of which will probably never be bested.
Move over Call of Duty Ghosts, Medal of Honor Warfighter and Battlefield 4. There's a new king in town and his name is Red Orchestra 2.

A Hat in Time... man oh man, what a journey it has been. Discovered this game two years a go I think; I became a "slacker backer" for it as soon as I discovered it. I've been following it ever since; played the heck out of Beta, played their Speedrunning Demo, and even though I have 100% this game already, I continue to keep playing it.
In A Hat in Time, you take control of an adorable protagonist simply named "Hat Kid." Hat Kid is stopped at a fairly unusual world as her fuel for her space ship, the Time Pieces, are taken from her. Hat Kid will have to jump and sprint her way across the planet to retrieve all of her Time Pieces, meeting a lot of whimsical characters along the way.
The game is a collectathon, so you'll find a variety of treasures in each level; some you'll find in large quantities, some you'll have to purchase, and others you'll have to hunt for.
If you've ever played literally any 3D Mario game, get this. You will be far from disappointed.

Blood and Bacon is a indie game that is unique to say the least. It may not be the most AAA title from popular developers, but that does not make this game just as good. Not only did this game meet my standards but also exceeded. This game when above and beyond the Call of Duty (which this game is nothing like).
Story- well to say the least of the story, there is one that i haven't exactly found out. This games story makes you really dig deep into the game, as they did not just do cut scenes and put the story out in the open. I personally like this approach to the game, as this makes the game more deep then you would think on first hand when playing the game.
Game play-The single player was fun to play through without cheats, although cheats are a totally viable option (if you want every day to be revenge day). I couldn't test the multi player as i didn't have any friends who play this game. However- they put in a whole alpha phase to the multi player (meaning it is currently being tested) and they put in a harder game mode for the multi player if you want to, along with server commands. If you have friends, play it with them, it will only make the game more enjoyable. Single player is just as fun however, so either way you can not go wrong. The weapons in the game are just as good as you would expect them to be in other shooters. They are balanced, fun and easy to use, and not one gun is better then the other, so its all based on how you want to play. Although the number of guns you get are small, this is a good thing, so you are not over whelmed with what to pick and choose. Hit boxes are up to standards with other games.  This game also has gore to it, as the title suggests, meaning body parts go flying if the enemy is shot the right way. You can also kick them and complete an achievement with them.
Sound-The sound in this game is very well made. This isn't a shooter that is supposed to be realistic, so don't go judging the game on that end. Instead, judge it on how clear the sound is. The sound is very clear  to say the least. There is also no sound delay, so you wont feel like the sound is lagging (this can be very frustrating)
Graphics-Although the graphics are not like Destiny or Fall Out 4 on the PC, this game is not supposed to be like that. The graphics were made to please the eye, while also being not so strong that you cant play it on non gaming or old PCs, or even a laptop. I got 60 Frames Per Second (FPS) while played this game every time I did. I never Experienced any lag except if I had a browser open while playing, but this is because my laptop is not the most graphically enhanced. This game is about the experience, and not the power about it (even an achievement for turning up the "graphics" lol).
Over all rating-If you like shooter games, this does not fall below even the most modern shooters. This game visually gives me a vibe of Retro games like Left 4 Dead, while still giving me a sensation that describes the most modern games.
This game could have easily been priced up to 30 dollars for how good it is, but the developers decided to put the game to just a dollar, to make a profit off of the game but still be affordable so everyone could play the game.
Rating 10/10. Recommended for people who like: Shooters, arcade games, multi player games, and value games.

At first, i always only noticed this game at every glance i had of it and sometimes saw it mentioned on other websites or Youtube videos. So i thought to myself: I have many games similar to this so why not try it out! So out went my money and in came the game into my library. I always enjoyed games that had this similar feel but was more comedy rather than plot development (If your know your Anime games on Steam you will know which ones im talking about) but still liked them in the end.
Tales of Zestiria is a great game and has quite the interesting plot. The more you progress, the more you learn about what the true problem of the story is and how the story begins to change to fit that new terror you begin to see. Unlike the other games i played, the plot has its more serious tone and even adds in some comedy to keep you entertained.
The characters are pretty well developed and have their own personalities to suit them. You obviously start with your main cast of Sorey and Mikleo, but find and learn more about the characters later in the story and begin to create a bond with these characters making you have feelings for them whenever a crisis has occured. Every characters has its part in the story,
.
Lastly the gameplay, as an impatient person i am i tend to hate the whole "Grinding, Equip, Shop etc" part but with this being a RPG i cant dislike something that makes the game challenging. With that being said, Tales of Zestiria has an amazing world map with many big to even huge landscape locations with tons of enemies to enjoy and kill. The combat is new to what i would expect in an RPG instead of the usual Turn-Base system. It can get pretty boring with its lack of Special Moves for you to use but that wont stop battles from being fun and challenging specially with the whole Artes idea and basically the games own "Transformation" like other RPGs like the Neptunia series "HDD" and Fairy Fencer's "Fairize" (Off topic but true).
Oh i forgot to mention DLC. The DLC can seem a little expensive to most (Im looking at you Adventure Items.....) but some are quite worth the payment. I would reccommend Alisha's Story DLC as it gives you some additional information on the story and characters. Though i would reccommend playing that extra chapter after completing the game entirely to help prevent any spoilers and to get a better understanding of the story.
In the end, this game is wonderful. As of hearing its part of a "Tales" franchise, i am quite excited to see what the other games are like. With the story being well thought out and relatable, if not great, characters that you meet and recruit to help your quest as a Sheperd. My rating for this game is a 8, if not 9 out of 10.

A Hat In Time is a fantastic platformer.  I never thought that any platformer would dethrone Voodoo Vince as my favorite, but after fourteen years it has happened.  A Hat In Time is a wonderfully cute game where no planets are the same.  You can be riding a train for one act, and the next one you are leading a marching band in a parade.  If I had to describe A Hat In Time, I would say it is a combination of Super Mario Sunshine, Mario Galaxy, and Banjo Kazooie.  The game takes what makes those three great and leaves out all that doesn't.  The soundtrack is so wonderful that I felt that I had to go and purchase it so I can listen to it while I play other games.  The upbeat nature of all the characters and music is enough to get anybody hooked.  At the time of writing this review, I only have eight hours and I have beat the story.  I usually consider story length to decide if a game is worth it, but in this case I judged the game's value off of fun factor.  I am currently working on hitting 100 percent, and I am having a fantastic time fooling around in the acts as I do so.
If I had to give this game a score, it would be a 10/10.  I absolutely love platformers, and this game has all the characteristics of a fantastic one.  The soundtrack, the characters, and the comedy all come together wonderfully.  For me, this has absolute potential to be my game of the year.
Edit : I have now gotten 100 percent completion, but not all the achievements.  I'm very excited for the community to start creating things for this game.

Banished is the most cathartic game I've ever played. During a particularly stressful time in my life this little gem popped up in the steam summer sale and has received most of my attention since.
In this game, you play an omnipotent and omnipresent overlord of a small and yearning-to-thrive midevil hamlet. Starting with a handful of people and a place to store goods, this simcity-like simulator encourages you to build your little hamlet from nothing into a bustling town. In the process, you need to manage your people's heath, happiness, hunger and warmth.
Banished is a very calming exercise. You have no invading hordes to worry about, no political alliances to manage and no trade routes to maintain. This is city management at its purest form. Like SimCity, you may have some disasters.. a sickness here, loss of crops there.. but these "disasters" are few and far between and often easily managed. (Though, admitted, I did have one early game in which a tornado decided to just roll right through my town killing all but 6 of my people.)
The goal here is to build. With building comes additional management. Placement becomes key. Pathing becomes a puzzle. Your little dominion grows into a bustling small town. Your blacksmiths tink tink tink the days away. The chatter of your folk is omnipresent. The harridness of the small town grows into a bustling small city.
This is your world. You created it.
Cathartic.
(Notes: The game has infinite replayability, like any city sim.. however it does support Steam Workshop and there's a lot of great stuff on there.)

Oh, and also you can't move the camera if you aren't holding one of the mouse buttons, the cursor is completely visible at all times, and if you have multiple monitors, the cursor does not lock to the one the game is on, meaning you can accidentally click off of the game.

When I was a little kid, I used to watch a cartoon called Rocket Power.  My favorite character in the show was Twister, for his great haircut.  I was always so inspired by the show that I too decided to ride skateboards in the skatepark.  I went out and spent $700 on buying different wheels for my skateboard, and ended up choosing the one's that were blue, for they were my favorite color at the time.  I threw out the rest of the wheels and headed for the skatepark that was located about seven miles from my house.  It was a long walk, but I knew it would all be worth it.  After my arrival, I headed up for the biggest ramp and made my first attempt.  I fell face first because I didn't put the wheels on correctly and my nose cracked and was bent in the wrong direction.  There was blood gushing everywhere and I thought I was going to die.  I was unable to see out of my left eye, so I thought something had happened to that as well.  Some kid came up to me and pulled out his cell phone and started to dial 911.  An ambulence soon arrived and I was taken to the emergency room.  At this point, I had passed out, but was told the rest of the story.  I had a broken nose and my left eye was dangling out of my head by it's optic nerve.  The doctors at the hospital placed my eyeball back in place without any hygenic precautions.  Once it was back in place, it was soon discovered that there was multiple infections, and that I would have to have my eye removed.  As of today, I have a disformed nose and only my right eye.  However, Just Cause 2 is good, and you should buy this game.

Kingpin Life of Crime, is a arcade style FPS that blends platforming elements, questing hubs, neutral and friendly NPC's and even a interaction voice command system effectively into an amazing game, and one you'll definatley want to pick up.
One thing you should know about Kingpin is it doesn't have a great story. Don't come into this expecting A thrilling plot with twists and turns. Kingpin starts off with your character, a nameless thug, left beaten in an alley in a ghetto named ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ by some cronies of a guy named Nicky, and being told to never enter a place called Poisonville again. From the now infamous "Im gonna bury those two ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s" to the ending, this game is a bland revenge tale told from cutscenes randomly placed in the game. You go on a chase to find Nicky and become the new Kingpin and gain respect. But half the time you don't even know who it is your even shooting at. But the story isn't the charm of the game, and the main appeal is either going to come from the violent combat, or from the sheer difficulty of the title.
The game uses profane lanuage most of the time with "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" this and "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" that. And follows up with brutal combat. Seriously, the wounds that appear on enemy corpses are just plain gory, and enemies leave a trail of blood when they move, which is useful for tracking down fleeing enemies, which is pretty impressive AI for the time. To add to this, Kingpin splits amor into various areas, like head, torso and legs. So natrually, you can shoot enemies body parts for different effects, like blowing limbs clean off. The game's shooting mechanics are nothing speacial, and amount to nothing for than pointing, and shooting, but the game is so goddamned difficult. Really, even on it's lower difficulty settings, this game will tear you a new one. You'll get your♥♥♥♥♥handed to you time and time again, but that's how we rolled back in the 90's and sometimes you'll just have to sigh and hit the quickload button. You die very easily in the game, and the enemies early on just are bullet sponges. There is no difficulty curve.
Kingpin Life of Crime is a great game, despite it's apparent flaws regarding it's story, and combat aspects, and I would reccomend it to anyone that enjoys old school shooters that are violent and difficult. Now get out there and bury some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s!

Pretty game, with excellent art direction and a brilliant sense of atmosphere.
Really fun managing the typical issues one faces in survival, shelter, water, food. It's nice having to keep track of injury as well as basic needs. Avoid injury, obviously.
The clothing and "crafting" mechanics are excellent as well, with the focus being on scavenging and maintenance versus creating. It definitely feels like a "survival" experience compared to the usual "Survival is actually thriving once you build a log cabin now get ready for zombies" experience.
All of that "Realism" holds up.
Why am I not recommending it?
I'm an outdoors guy, I love being out in the woods, and the Long Dark was offering me a realistic zomibe-free, plausible senario to simulate survival in. It's awesome at those things.
The wildlife is frustratingly unrealistic and it wasn't until after I booted up the game that I was informed (maybe that's my fault, but this information was never obvious to me so it still counts) "We're not trying to make realistic wildlife."
That was annoying. Because wildlife is a reasonably integral part of a wilderness experience.
The most gruelling issue is that wolves are the size of coyotes, they seem to travel alone a LOT (not really how wolves roll,) and they attack you on sight.
This was a disappointing and important part for me, and it ruined the game for me pretty much.
For people who wont get bugged by details like that, I suggest you go for it, by all other accounts it seems pretty spot on.
For people who, like me, were hoping for something refreshing and more "realistic" from the usual survival gig, I'd not suggest it.

I've never written a review on steam before, but after putting over 18 days worth of hours into this thing I thought maybe I should, haha.
Having absolutely NO experience developing any sort of video game I bought this on a whim when my friend told me it was on sale. I was instantly consumed with learning how to work the thing. It's interesting, because it does the literal language coding for you, but you still have to put the sentances together. Sort of like not knowing a language but having a dictionary and a vague idea of the grammar structure. Map by map, event by event, I understood more and more how to communicate what I wanted to the computer. HOURS of trial and error.
But eventually it all starts to really come together and I started doing cooler and cooler things. Neat puzzles and push blocks and mazes and timed races, personality quizzes, you name it. I'd challenge myself by picturing a scene, what would be REALLY cool if it happened in that scene and then spending six hours figuring out how to pull it off. (I'm a fan of the dramatic so I've pulled off some real harrowing cutscenes for a pixel style game like this hahaha).
It only exports to Windows and that sucks, and since it's older than MV there aren't as many cool scripts and no one is updating them anymore. There aren't as many tileset options as MV and the tile boxes are smaller which kinda sucks. But it goes on sale more and depending on how professional you want to get with this it works just fine. Plus, it comes with LOADS of preset and balanced abilities, weapons, monsters, heroes and classes, which is nice for beginners (took me ages to figure out how to balance a good battle system). It's easy to customize and it has a good "Create a character/sprite" sort of function. And BEST it's fairly user friendly in that if you hover your mouse over almost anything in the entire program it will give you at least a base explanation of what it is. 90% reason why I learned how to use it.
A lot of people say it's only good for making run of the mill JRPG games but it just takes a little imagination to make it totally original. I made a game about a 6th grader and her main weapon was her blankie. Just put some thought into it.

My first little "review" on Steam, even though I won't be going into that much detail.
I grew up with 3D platformers on N64 and really still love these kinds of games the most. Nowadays I usually have a hard time getting excited to play any kind of game, but I really really liked Yooka-Laylee, which is also a new nostalgic like 3d platformer. Many people spoke badly of that game and while I can understand the flaws, I really enjoed it.
Anyway, now my good friend told me about this and even gave his second steam code he had for free. Thanks so much again! I will probably support later myself and buy the PS4 version eventually!
So I heard it was also a traditional platformer, but a bit more modern.
And that's just what this is! Very much feels like games in the old days, but more modern when it comes to objectvies and less collectables! Not that I hate collecting things in these games.
So what aspects stand out in this game? One important aspect that will have a lot of influence in the enjoyment of a game like this, the controls! And they are perfect! They just feel natural and you are just in control. Nothing more to add, turned out very good. Even the dreaded camera for games like these is very solid at least! Rarely and problems at all!
Then, the artstyle! Very cute, by the way I really liked the main character, so adorable and with a lot of charm. The colors just pop and...you just feel at home in the worlds. Great atmosphere. The music is very fitting too!
The missions in the game are for the most part very creative and the concepts change all the time! Some have you exlpre mainly, others mix things up a lot by having you confronted with creepy characters that even claim your soul, or a murder mystery! Funny writing too!
The challenges this game offers are enjoyable and very fair, in fact I could say one of the slightly negative aspects is that this game is a bit too easy. Other than some of the bosses, but I really am not good at them, they stress me out and in general I hate bosses in video games, I rarely had any issues. I even went for all achievements which offered some nice challenges!
Also, the game is unfortunately a bit on the short side, a few more worlds would have been nice, but apparently DLC is coming! Same as a Co-Op mode? Can't wait to play this again together with my friend!
So yeah, amazing game with a lot of charme, I am so glad this was recommended to me, so well here you go, I do the same by sharing my opinion in this review.
Thanks for reading! Please go try out this game!
Rating: 9.5/10

As a remaster, this appears to be done rather well. It looks more crisp than it did in the disc version of the game I played before, and everything seems to control like it did then, etc. I loved this game when it first came out. However, I tried playing it again a while after that (on disc, years ago), and it didn't appeal to me at all. The characters are a bit wooden at times, the story and direction starts out pretty entertaining but gets so zany that it betrays the otherwise seriousness of its own tone, in my opinion.
Moreover, the biggest issue, I think, is that most of us are tired of excessive quick-time events. I'm not completely turned off by mashing a button to open a vent in Arkham Asylum or anything like that, no. However, Fahrenheit: Indigo Prophecy has scenes that have very long quick-time events with tons of button prompts. I'm not even complaining that they're difficult. I didn't have problems.
It's just that I realized I was not having fun because the game is not designed so that you really feel like you're controlling a character, so much as it's designed to feel like you are pressing buttons hardly related to what your character is doing. There was a massive disconnect between myself and feeling like I had any sense of agency in the game itself. So I would say that between this issue and the insane storyline conflicting with the tone of the game, I cannot recommend this game.
I don't really like consoles, but if you want a game with similar elements that has a story and characters I much preferred, I would say to play Heavy Rain. David Cage made it, too, but I thought it was much better, though not without its flaws.

One of my favourite ever shooters. I bought this game for about £3 - the price of a pint of beer. What a buy it was. It has provided me with hundreds of hours of gritty, immersive and extremely atmospheric gameplay. I love this game because it rewards noble gameplay: Patience, perseverance, precision, wit - compared to the homogenised, soft - edged generic excuses for FPSs that we are now spoon fed.
Yes, at first you will get shot from 150m countless times by someone you think must be invisible or hacking. Yes you will be frustrated at constantly being blown in to disgusting flesh lumps by artillery. Yes you will be annoyed that you can't be a sniper every match and are forced to use a boring bolt action rifle with iron sights.
However once you master the rifleman class the whole game starts to fall into place and you will realise that this is one of the best and most "different" tactical experiences you have ever had.
9.5/10 I love this game and would absolutely recommend it if you are an experienced FPS player looking for more depth. However if you are a 14 year old with no patience, don't even bother.

This is an interesting little game. It's a bit like Sim City in that all you are really doing is resource collecting and managing a little town. It also reminds me of that aspect of Black & White.
The problem I am running into however, is that the game gets a bit boring since there's no "real" conflict such as needing to keep a militia ready in case of invasion, or even dangerous animals, or upgrading technologies. The only real "danger" is from starving, freezing, getting sick, fires, or tornados.
You also have to watch out for doing too much too fast, because while your first winter is creeping up, your townsfolk would rather go out chopping resources you may already have enough of, to drop materials off on buildings you have on HOLD (meaning your builders won't build them), rather than build the buildings you need to keep firewood or FOOD going throughout the bad times.
If you can wait for another Steam Sale and it's a couple bucks, pick it up. But you gotta be a certain kind of person to be able to deal with this game for any length of time.

This is a good game, but is not perfect, nor original.  Though there are alot of good things about it, but I cant say I am too excited about it.  I say that, in just having completing it and found that I can genuinely say that I do 'like' the game,
So what was so good about Outlast?
Well, I will have to say that it's Amnesia!  I loved Amnesia and any game that emulates that legend is good in my books.  Red Barrels have done a good job of making a Pacifist, survival horror game and have done well of making a relative carbon copy of that original game.
There also are hallmarks of Silent hill all over it.
I can sometimes smell a bit of Wolfentstein too(The return to Castle Wolfenstein)... or maybe just the Nazi/WW2 usual feel to it... inparticular the music has alot of the same orhcestral broken up thumping ,with alot of 'stringy' Melanchole too, though it is different throughout and the ambient sound does help the game alot.
Some levels remind me of Penumbra too...
The story... Yea  it was good... As in I could not have predicted the end result (like Amnesia: tDD).  I guess the scripts (notes thoughout game) help, but generally you could play without it I suppose, its worth reading if your into that sort of thing (like me).
The control and the engine work and are nice.  Hell, I'd hope so as it's run on the Unreal engine; everythign feels smooth and I did not feel one glitch.
It looks quite nice too, not quite the walkthrough Gallery 'Amnesia 2 -Mahcine for Pigs' was but the art design looks nicely done.
A few things I did not like about Oulast:
The teasers gave me the impression that it was going to be scary( though I knew it was Amnesia anyway) and even that it was going to be more action packed and perhaps progessive than Amnesia was.  however, it is not.  It runs at the same pace as said game, and is simplier.  These people have made a good copy. As flattering as that sounds...
The Simpler thing is something to be expanded; Its not only simpler, but completely Linear.  The Level Design is Complex, but Linear, as in its like one of those maze games in the paper, where there is only one way, and even worse, there is much less need to explore and the game doesn't appear to reward .  All loot (batteries) appears to be based whether I was low on them(I am certain), so there doesn't appear to be any reward for exploring at all, which is pretty weak.
The interaction with objects thing too is more linear too; only specific objects can be interacted with and there are few of them around,similar perhaps to Amnesia 2(Machine for Pigs).  There are a few additional and different dynamics to Amnesia, such as mantling (jumping up to climb on to a high object) and side stepping on ledges.
Just like Amnesia, the AI is very Dull, I guess I am not complaining... But I have had some instances where I have been standing in light in front of a foe and still I was not seen.  Amnesia was very unforgiving, once you were struck, generally you were dead, which made it feel even more exhilarating when being chased, but this one is not quite like that.  You can run around in loops and get hit, sometimes 5 times and still run off and jump in to vent, and be so happy this is easier :P. Though I played this on Normal I think.. Guess I should play it on insane and then rethink... As there are 4 difficulty settings, making it more accessible perhaps?
I think this game is worth buying in all, it was a good expereince to be played and I enjoyed it and would give the time for another play through (if I've got the time). Also I would not have thought that a game like this would have been made by the people who made such mainstream games(Assassin's Creed, Prince of Persia), but they did, so credit to them.
I will note though if you do play this, you should probably give it some time before you drop it completely( I found this rather dull at first... but it grew on me, until I hit a third of the way in and felt like I was getting sucked in...)This is a game of immersion, just like Amnesia.  Give it the time and it should reward; if at least with story.

Bioshock is interactive art in every sense of the word. From its breathtaking art deco scenery to it's disturbing, deep story, Bioshock succeeds where countless others have failed. Bioshock will take you on an underwater thrill ride that will leave you breathless, shaking and satisfied in a curious, perhaps even morbid way. It forces you to really think about the events and people, even long after you've beaten the game. And any game capable of such a feat is a must-buy in my opinion.

Here are some survival hints for a long and happy life:
- if you are not already there, travel to the coastal highway - it's like paradise compared to mystery lake
- keep attention to the calories/bullet ratio: if you wait for a wolf to attack a deer, walk up to him and give him a head shot, you can have about 14 kg of meat (wolf+fresh deer) for just one bullet. Just don't miss.
- don't waste energy. Instead of force-sleeping when not tired, you can repair, harvest, forage or melt snow. You can use the time needed for this on other occasions.
- if you want to evade wolves safely, seek low, plain ground, so you can see them from afar. they often jump "out of nowhere", becuase they are behind a hill where you cannot see them
- eating older meat gives risk of food poisoning. it will wreck your whole day
- if you're keen on thorough exploration, draw a map on paper
- harvest newspaper rolls

It's amazing but short. It has a simple silent story that doesn't push you along or guide you by the hand. It just gives you the path for you to run down. It's good at being creepy without pushing into terror which leaves you on the edge for so much longer then most games. The puzzles are simple at first, then they build and get more interesting and clever.
-Pros-
1: Short in a good way, doesn't over extend itself and it has the right style to be replayable.
2: Perfect Atmosphere, has overall feeling of being alone in this stark world with ways to die everywhere which helps give you a reason to go foward with small flirtations with hope, intrigue, and near fright.
3: Story, nice and simple to the point where it doesn't even need words to get it... some words would be a tad nice however.
4: Clever and simple puzzles with a good difficulty curve.
5: A stark black and white visual gives it a unique feel and gives the game it's own kind of beauty.
-Cons-
1: Should establish the story a bit more i think. A small message at the beginning or something. It isn't a huge con because i understand why it isn't included. But i don't think one small nudge would of ruined it and it could help with the motivation.
I honestly thought i'd be able to think of more Cons... but to be honest i can't. For everything it was going for it did. It wasn't perfect, nothing is, but it's pretty damn close in my opinion. Worth many replays, since i got it it's been a halloween tradition to play it again. It's size bugs at me a bit to be honest. Because it is short which is normally a bad thing... but in this game it's a perfect length so it's hard to count it as bad.

Hey! A playable demo of Super Mario Odyssey before it comes out! Seems to include a big portion of the game. Few complaints about this demo. First, Mario doesn't really look like Mario. Also, what happened to Cappy? It's just replaced with other hats to cover it up. I was excited for the mechanic of Capturing! Why did they remove it?
Although, I must say I am intrigued by all of the new characters it brings. This demo makes it seem like a completely different aesthetic! Adding a Mafia that are just a bunch of bad cooks? Ingenious! This game also features full voice acting, even for Mario! And most of it seems to give you a general idea on who a character is, which is needed considering the ton of new characters like DJ Grooves and the Snatcher. Not to mention the plethora of cosmetics that Mario can wear. The sound is also a great feature, and it goes the full mile to be great.
All in all, I think this Odyssey demo is definitely what the fans want. It expands greatly upon the Mario Universe, with a new planet in play. This game DOES have a few graphical errors, though. Not what I expected from a triple-a Mario title. but I'll live. Get this 30 dollar demo. You won't regret it.

this game is awesome, I play a frigate which is easily the hardest ship to play. the game is a building moba with classes. unlike other building mobas, you don't have to stockpile parts. just unlock them with "junk". you do have to try and level your classes up though, which increases the amount of parts you can build a ship out of. at lvl 10, you will be able to upgrade parts with junk. the game has a money currency, but it's mostly to buy decorations. space whiskey and pilot license can be bought to ramp up how much exp and junk you earn in battles
classes:
frigates are fast but easily destroyed. they also recently recieved a damage nerf, so focus on being fast and supporting your team with abilities. typically best way for winning with frigates now is to capture the points and then upgrade them so those mines can rack up kills for you. good players won't fall for that but bots always will.
battleships are your slow, lumbering beasts. good damage means they want to be in the middle of fights. really good at defending capture points
cruisers are the real support class. abilities a plenty. otherwise they have fairly even stats.
destroyers are the big damage dealers. if you like being a sniper, be a destroyer. they got better range than anyone. other than that, they are easy to destroy so they really like that sniping position out of range from other players. the recent game changes has made it hard for destroyers to function well for the team as the game is no longer about kills but capturing points.
the game has bots to fill vacant spaces in matches. you can tell which ones are bots by looking at the kind of ships that can be bought (a new mechanic I don't really get into). bought ships generally are subpar to hand crafted ships but they help give you an idea of how to build

Great software, I like all the DLC content and it is really easy to use. If you're stuck on something and are not quite sure how to do something, there is a lot of help out there on media channels on this game and tutorials. If you have a creative mind and just want to whip up something quick and fun, or even a longer more in depth game, then RPG Maker VX Ace is what you want. No programming skills needed, although you do need to understand how certain sequences work.  This can be easily learned though through experience playing the game or watching tutorials.  There are also scripts out there that can be implemented into the game to enhance the game or change the flow of it which is always fun.  The variety of characters and scenes in this game vary, from bubbly traditional RPGs to darker animated sprites and enemies depending on the DLC a user purchases.  I believe the programming language used is Ruby, so if a user is studying this language or wants to learn it, might be a good way to mess with the programming and learn. DLC is not automatically implemented into the game files of each game, you have to manually go into the directory and add the DLC to the current game a user is constructing, this must be done for every project as far as I know. Happy game making, hope this helped!

My first little "review" on Steam, even though I won't be going into that much detail.
I grew up with 3D platformers on N64 and really still love these kinds of games the most. Nowadays I usually have a hard time getting excited to play any kind of game, but I really really liked Yooka-Laylee, which is also a new nostalgic like 3d platformer. Many people spoke badly of that game and while I can understand the flaws, I really enjoed it.
Anyway, now my good friend told me about this and even gave his second steam code he had for free. Thanks so much again! I will probably support later myself and buy the PS4 version eventually!
So I heard it was also a traditional platformer, but a bit more modern.
And that's just what this is! Very much feels like games in the old days, but more modern when it comes to objectvies and less collectables! Not that I hate collecting things in these games.
So what aspects stand out in this game? One important aspect that will have a lot of influence in the enjoyment of a game like this, the controls! And they are perfect! They just feel natural and you are just in control. Nothing more to add, turned out very good. Even the dreaded camera for games like these is very solid at least! Rarely and problems at all!
Then, the artstyle! Very cute, by the way I really liked the main character, so adorable and with a lot of charm. The colors just pop and...you just feel at home in the worlds. Great atmosphere. The music is very fitting too!
The missions in the game are for the most part very creative and the concepts change all the time! Some have you exlpre mainly, others mix things up a lot by having you confronted with creepy characters that even claim your soul, or a murder mystery! Funny writing too!
The challenges this game offers are enjoyable and very fair, in fact I could say one of the slightly negative aspects is that this game is a bit too easy. Other than some of the bosses, but I really am not good at them, they stress me out and in general I hate bosses in video games, I rarely had any issues. I even went for all achievements which offered some nice challenges!
Also, the game is unfortunately a bit on the short side, a few more worlds would have been nice, but apparently DLC is coming! Same as a Co-Op mode? Can't wait to play this again together with my friend!
So yeah, amazing game with a lot of charme, I am so glad this was recommended to me, so well here you go, I do the same by sharing my opinion in this review.
Thanks for reading! Please go try out this game!
Rating: 9.5/10

I have very mixed feelings about this game. Some parts of it are just amazing - /some/ music, /some/ writing, /some/ world-building, but then there's a lot of lazy writing, astoundingly bad character development and poor choices of musical theme. In terms of gameplay - the minigames only feel right when there's an action sequence - they actually make it seem like the graphics are better than they really are; the standard adventure walk-and-click segments are decent, save for a few moments when you're on a timer and the camera angle is awful, and everything else is a frustrating chore.
Get it, but bear in mind this is more of an experiment in what would later become 'telltale' games, rather than a well-polished experience something modern would provide.

There’s something eerie, almost supernatural about winter in the far North. Night that seems to last forever, feeling your breath start to freeze in your lungs, the crunch of hard-packed snow under your boots. Sometimes I miss the long winter nights of Canada and the stillness they bring. The Long Dark is a survival experience that brings me back to my youth in Canada’s frozen north.
Hinterland Studio’s first person survival sim is currently in early access. At the moment the alpha only offers a sandbox mode but there’s a story mode in development for later releases. How does The Long Dark compare to similar games and what are my initial impressions?
In a lot of ways The Long Dark reminds me of other survival-related games like Minecraft and Day Z. You start in a random location and explore a static map (unlike Minecraft’s procedurally generated worlds), scavenging for food, water, and safety from the hostile environment.
In The Long Dark this appears to be the most dangerous aspect. Sure, there are dangerous animals like wolves running around, but you’re more likely to be killed by the cold or hunger than eaten by a wolf. You need to juggle basic needs by eating, drinking, sleeping, and seeking shelter from the cold. You can forage for firewood, repair your clothing, and hunt the local wildlife (if you manage to find a rifle and ammo).
Unlike Day Z, however, I didn’t feel a great sense of momentum when playing The Long Dark. Maybe it’s the lack of external threat in the form of other players or the fact you start with a full set of winter clothing. I spent most of my time exploring the wilderness, looking for interesting landmarks, and trying not to starve to death. At the moment I don’t see a lot of replayability in the sandbox mode, but that could change with later releases.
Unlike Minecraft, a game that combines building with exploration, I don’t feel any need to keep playing The Long Dark for more than one or two sessions at a time. I see how long I can survive and then laugh when I get mauled to death or fall off a cliff. I’m looking forward to seeing the story mode, and finding out if the narrative will keep me playing.
The Long Dark looks amazing. The visuals are striking and the game itself feels really polished. If this is an alpha I can’t wait to see future releases. The minimal HUD, sound design, and art style all serve to create an atmosphere of cold and isolation. The only human contact I’ve had so far is stumbling across frozen bodies half-buried in the snow.
There’s a lot of promise here: good survival systems, amazing visuals, and memorable setting. However, at the moment there’s not much in The Long Dark to keep my interest in the long term. I’ve enjoyed my time playing but I see the alpha as an extended demo. I can’t wait to see what the full game develops into as at the moment it feels a little sparse.
The Long Dark brings me back to my childhood; memories of trudging through the cold, the silence, and the darkness. Like the real Canadian winter, however, The Long Dark is best experienced in short increments.

RPG Maker VX Ace is the seventh in a series of RPG Makers going back to 1992. It allows for the easy creation of a Japanese-style RPG without having to know how to write code. For those who can write code, the newer engines provide a scripting language that allows the developer to modify nearly every aspect of the game.
For those who want to express themselves though a game but are not able to write code from scratch, RPG Maker is a great tool. You can just draw your maps, define all your weapons/armors/enemies/etc., and place your events, using a menu-driven tool for defining what each event does. Even this simplified system can be very powerful as the user gains experience using it.
For those who want a little more power, RPG Maker VX Ace uses a Ruby Scripting language which is pretty easy to use once you figure out the data structures and functions. Those who already know how to program in an object-oriented language should have little trouble learning RSS. The Help File includes most of the information needed to get started.

To put it simply: A Hat in Time makes Yooka Laylee look like a Newgrounds game.
To be more exact: This game is a masterpiece and without a doubt the best game of 2017. It is one of the rare occurances of a Kickstarter game succeeding. It might even be the best Kickstarted game ever.
There was never a point in this game where I wasnt compeled or bored. There are things in every act that you didn't see before, or didn't explore a certain way and things will leave you having eureka moments constantly. The controls are to the point and feel amazing with an Xbox One controller. Any time I messed up a jump or missed a ledge, it was my own fault and not the game. When you made a hard jump you felt rewarded and usually were rewarded. The difficulty progressed with you, and the game opened up to multiple acts, allowing you to tackle harder objectives early if you wanted. Each boss took about 2-3 tries for me, mainly due to not paying attention or not knowing the mechanics the first time. The boss battles can be a little long.
The story is cute and the characters are fun, unique and engaging. The acts all differ and have their own stories, charm and mechanics. Subcon forest is one that I think back to a lot. It's impressive. This game is everything Super Mario Sunshine is and could ever be. I dare say that A Hat in Time could rival Super Mario Odyssey (a game im looking forward to) as the best collectathon platformer this year.

Some of you may heard of games such as Heavy Rain or Beyond: Two Souls. These two are made by the same company and designer as Fahrenheit: Indigo Prophecy. Now, the thing is that all three are interactive drama story based games, where the player can affect the flow of the story by their actions. And in Indigo Prophecy it's not like it matters much - it usually changes just a bit of details in a way so minor, that the ending depends only on your final decision, and
of the decisions made prior to the final stage will affect it.
Fahrenheit starts off pretty strong and promising, telling you a story of a mysterious murder, giving you control over a total of three characters. But, as the plot goes on, writing comes more and more weak, cliches turn in, and soon you understand that the whole concept of the plot was based on them. And in the end it all feels so cheesy and soft, so tasteless, that the game just leaves you alone in disgust. That is what happened to me, of course.
To the technical details, the graphics component is... tolerable, depending on how sensitive your eyes are. The audio, overall, is alright, except for some instances of weird voice acting. And the controls... well, you won't even need them most of the time, only for quick time events, where you have to use WASD and Arrow keys. Almost every interaction is handled by a mouse, and sometimes it is quite frustrating. The game has controller support, and if you have one, you better use that instead.
David Cage, the head of Quantic Dream, the writer and designer of Fahrenheit, is notorious for his notable writing. If you are wondering about getting a decent interactive action-adventure drama story based game, and you have a PlayStation 3, consider buying Heavy Rain instead. However, this piece, even though it's a classic, is not worth it.
The game itself is presented quite poorly, and with the exception of a few enjoyable moments, is just a pile of cliche garbage from David Cage. With the outdated graphics it has, Fahrenheit: Indigo Prophecy, despite being a classic, is not worth neither your time nor your money.

For me, I knew what was coming when I saw Angelo Badalmenti's name in the credits. All the works I've seen with his music, from Twin Peaks to Mulholland Drive, have started normal and turned strange by the end credits. But I always come around to loving the material, being hooked from an interesting start and becoming intrigued as the plot thickens into what it does.
Fahrenheit is the exact same way. With a gripping start to a very pecular end game, I was hooked. The characters and mystery had me wondering what was happening from the very beginning, from the opening murder that gave me chills to the revelations that had me in a strange form of suspense. It's certainly a unique tale by the end, one I think should be experienced and not spoiled, but whether that use of "unique" is good or bad is up for personal opinion.
What I did not expect was the style of gameplay. This was my third experience with Quantic Dream (following playing Heavy Rain and Omikron: The Nomad Soul) and this almost had a middle ground between the two. It had the simple almost Telltale Games style of gameplay of Heavy Rain, but with the diversity of Omikron. This, however, was not always a good thing. Several segments, like the police station with Carla and the opening murder scene with Lucas, stuck out as very memorable. Others, like the flashback stealth segments, were downright frustrating, but kept me enthralled in the story nonetheless.
For $10, I don't think there's much to complain with value. It's a decent length game (at least 6 hours) with unlockable bonus content, as well as different endings and different gameplay choices that give some form of replay value. If Fahrenheit seems interesting, there's no loss in trying it. Just expect things to get real strange as Fahrenheit reaches its boiling point.

Cute/silly fun, well balanced, challenging, slightly tedious.
I bought it during the 50% off sale just to give it a try. My first time playing, I enjoyed it enough that I played for almost three hours straight.
Some people have mentioned a problem launching the game, but I haven't encountered that, nor any other problems.
I get why some people are getting stuck. Near the beginning, your progress will be a crawl unless you do the two mini games at least once each. Once you do this, you're able to buy some upgrades that make the battles go much better. Once you get a few upgrades, the battles themselves will give you all the money you need. They're very well balanced so that it's a tough challenge to come out ahead on money, but if you plan it right, you will.
The mini games are just silly phone-app type games that are a bit monotonous, but they're not terrible. They're just there as a way for you to earn extra money IF you need to. They help to ensure that you won't be stuck if you can't come out ahead in the battles. In one, you have to feed the cats in a dumbed down version of a diner game. In the other, you have to scoop their litter box. The only real challenge or interest in the litter box game is just seeing how fast you can rack up the money and how many hidden treasures you can find.
There's also a spy-dog on the main screen who offers to sell you items at very high prices. I found out by accident that once you buy these, they are permanently available to you in the main game at a small cost. Once you can buy some of these, it makes getting to higher waves in the main game much easier, which means you'll gain plenty of money in every battle.
At $2.50, I consider this a great buy. It's cheesy fun, something different.  $5 is probably about just right for this game if it speaks to you, but if you can get it on sale, I recommend it even if you're just somewhat curious.
