Having played Tales of Symphonia and enjoying it, and some of the VERY early ones like Tales of Phantasia I was hoping that this would be a more modern take on the JRPG genre. Unfortunately it is not, it is just a lot of bland environments stitched together with some mundane dialogue at best.
The dialogue to one side the combat system is awful, the majority of it can be summed up as "mash B button". You can swap mobs and do SLIGHTLY different moves (i.e press A button once then mash B again, or press R1 to become some superman and press B some more), but generally its clunky, its given you a 3d space to run around in, but you always just run in to fight a single monster, it would have felt far better if it just allowed you to run around and attack like an action game given the way the camera and attacks act, you also end up often getting shanked in the back in battles as you are too busy mashing B on the guy in front to notice you have twerked your way into the stragglers.
The story so far is at best bland, at worse boring and mundane. I quite like the idea of these celesial beings humans cannot see, but they just all feel like space cadets. For those of you who could stand enough of FF13 to meet Vanille will know what I am on about. Every time the characters open their mouth its just some random piece of nonsense they throw out and the animations are often clunky, like there is a bit early on where the seraphim with you shouts "BOO" at someone, and it was just animated in a really odd way and it just felt overly childish.
Anyway I could rant for longer, I am told it gets better after the 10 hour mark, currently I have far better games to play that would give me far more enjoyment and not require 10 hours investment for POSSIBLE good story/characters/fun.
If you like pressing the B button, this is a game for you.
If you do not like pressing B, I would stay away.

Unlike TSP the story isn't very interactive and the design is fairly linear. The interactivity and choice/consequence portion is non-existant. For $11.00, Canadian, you're more or less paying for basic interaction, proceding linearly through the level, and a narration. This isn't necesarilly a bad thing for those that enjoy story heavy elements such as myself. For those looking for the choices and hillarity associated with TSP wait for another release. But for those wanting a different experience with an interesting story and don't mind linear gameplay I'd recomend.

I cannot recommend this game in its current state as it has several flaws; as of Oct. 11, 2015.
One major flaw: Bugs. The game has crashed several times on me while playing one of the "mini-games". In this mini-game you clean the communal cat litter box. You essentially shovel excrement when it pops up in the litter box and while shoveling you can happen to find all sorts of items... or get nothing its a cr*p shoot. If you are not shoveling, then you are spraying to rid the communal litter box of stench.
The game has crashed on me consistently when shoveling when clicking moderately fast. And crashed once while spraying the stench. Others have reported it crashing while clearing waves. Fortunately, that didn't happen to me. This would be extremely painful as there is no auto-saving. So, if the game closes while clearing waves, then you lost all of the progress. You have to complete all of the waves or exit the current wave and Save to keep all of your progress.
The other flaw is Design/Ideas. As with other tower defense games, you can unlock and upgrade your defense units. This game has a one time purchase feature with a buff for all of your units versus upgrades for individual units. These upgrades are accomplished with money. As it is a tower defense game, you would think the majority of your money could be made with clearing waves.... Unfortunately this is not the case, at least not in the beginning. The mini-games was where I made the most money. There are two. One is a kind of "feed your troops" game which I was a little confused about at first as there was no mention of what to do. I did figure it out, but you can only attempt this mini-game after clearing some waves. A decent amount of money can be made from this. However, this presents some difficulty as you need money to purchase upgrades to progress further.
The other mini-game is maintaining the litter box, which I mentioned has problems above. It has been frustrating to try to save money for upgrades only to have it crash and lose all the time attempting to dig for gold. Why is this one of the main ways to make money in a tower defense game? Also, there are items that you can only find while digging in the litter box, you cannot purchase these in a store. The only way to purchase these items is if you unlock the airlift support feature and then the items you can purchase are completely random. When these items are purchased, you must immediately use them; you can't save the items for when you need them.
There is a feature to increase the speed of the game.... by one speed. For some of the bosses, dealing with them is very tedious and you wish there was an increase speed button to increase the speed even more to get through. As once my units where established, there was nothing else for me to do but sit and watch my units slowly decrease the bosses health bar.
I did eventually beat the game without getting all the upgrades. Tip to beat the game: get lots of items from the litter box. After I did, it unlocked one of the modes. However, this disabled the ability to level up my units as they were upgraded to the maximum level. The achievements for this game require you to reach the max level for upgrades. This is no longer possible with my current game. There is no feature to start a new game; I would have to uninstall the game and then reinstall it or clear the saved files for the game. All things I have to do outside the game, not in the game. As all my units are fully upgraded and no other upgrades are available, money becomes useless. There is nothing to strive for aside from trying to clear as many waves as possible, which just becomes tedious as some of the bosses just take time to kill. You can just walk away and come back and the boss will be dead. A few of the bosses do take effort. But overall, this game in its current state doesn't have me wanting more.
I will say I did have one interesting experience. I was listening to music while maintaing the communal litter box when some epic music songs started playing. Shoveling cat excrement while listening to epic music was interesting and took some of the dullness out of what I was doing.
Synopsis: Don't buy in its current state. It becomes tedious to play. Granted the game is cheap, if you do purchase the game, don't set your expectations high.

Banished is a game that throws you right into the middle of fight for survival. However, this fight isn't your typical fight. Its a fight against the elements.
From the start you're given a few families with barely anything, and you're tasked to shelter, provide, and watch over your exiles. In the begining you have enough resources to take care of their immediate concerns, but those resources soon run out. With winter fast approaching your concern for lumber and food rises. You begin asking yourself is there enough food; is there enough fuel; are there enough houses availabel? Just as Autumn passes and winter satrts knocking at your door, you are tasked with putting the fate of your village on the line. As the winter rages on and food and fuel dwindle down you find yourself nervous. And as winter peaks with your margin narrowly positive you realize that everything has worked out. With your first winter done you can now enjoy the game, until next winter that is...
Overall I find the game to be a very relaxing and pleasent game. It requires a good amount of thinking, but it's not to much to enjoy the game. Its very simple and has great mechanics. Just when you think the game is getting old the mods (via steam and other sites) really help to get you back into it, and the community for the game is great as well.

You don't have an hud to show you, for instance, how many bullets do you have so you have to GUESS, or better, KEEP THE COUNT of how many bullets you have available in the clip!
Not Enought!!! Not Enought!!! The main weapon, the weapon possessed by the most of the player in any match, is a BOLT-ACTION rifle! Not a damned every-situation assault rifle with laser aim, grenade launcher, earth detector, radar, double clip, triple zoom, and super stable aim!!!
There are so many aspect I can tell you but I don't want to extend too much this review. just another one: If you want to try it, it is often in sale for 1.75€!!! What else you want?!?

Want to survive in The Long Dark? Too bad. The game wants to kill you and it will do so in many different ways.
You will starve to death.
You will die of thirst.
You will freeze to death.
You will be eaten by wolves.
You will be eaten by more wolves.
Did I mention that you'll be eaten by wolves?
The Long Dark pulls no punches and gives no handouts. It is a game that will chill you to the core and freeze you to the bone. Once you enter this snowy expanse of woods, you will turn on survival mode. You will become the character you control. Your stomach will grumble when your character is hungry. You will shiver when your character is cold.
Best of all - you will jump for joy the first time you find a gun. A gun in this game is a new house, new clothes, and a new way of life. But don't take it for granted -- you will still die.
I recommend The Long Dark for anyone and everyone. This game is unique, immersive, and best of all, fun. You literally FEEL the fear that your character portrays when his/her heart starts thumping after spotting a wolf that's a little too close for comfort. You will be chilled, thrilled, and killed in this survival game.

I have taken sometime to play this game myself and I decided that I should write a review here so that it would be helpful for those who read it and decide whether to purchase this game or not.
Get to the point, right now the game is in 'Early Access' so it is not really complete. However, personally, only what the Early Access has offered now worths the money.
The very first thing that can be accounted as pros is the the game's very own concept. It is a new dimension of 'survival game', unlike many mainstream survival game lists which involve zombies and mutants to horrify you, this game is another story: just you against the 'Mother Nature'. You are on your own, among the cold, hunger, thirst, tiredness, or even danger from wolves. All you need to do is 'survive'. It sounds simple and uninteresting, but believe me this game is well enough even with this simplicity in this game genre. No safe place with lots of supplies (unless you choose 'Pilgrim' mode). You need to take risks with your own actions. Everything is by yourself.
The gameplay ... I don't know if I should classify it as a pro or con, but it is mixed. You can never expect anything from each playthrough; when you restart, everything except the regions will be resetted. This gives you the survival experience to some extends. For example, you might find a rifle, the only 'real' weapon in the game, without any bullets before you find one bullet miles away, or you need a can opener but still yet to be found; what will you do? which way? where is it going to be? Everything which other survival games may overlook matters in this game. You need clothes to keep you warm, raw food, if not cooked well, can be a threat when eaten, or you can even hurt your legs if you do not watch your steps (which happens to me a lot lol). These are some of the situations that I found and I need to give the 'thumb up' for the developer's careful planning so as to make this game as realistc as possible.
However, there is something that still bugs me; the wolves. They still lack realistic movements: too repetitive and can be easy to deal with as you get get used to the game. Even though the developer has mentioned something about the wolves, their movements and some behaviors, such as how slow or fast it should be in different situations, are needed for consideration *for developers*. I hope if the wolves are readjusted in the right way it would gives me more exciting experience. Nevertheless, even with this comment I still find dealing with wolves sometimes hard anyway. (I heard that more wildlife will be added, so it might be the solution for this problem as well.)
If you are fans of survival game and need a new dimension on survival experience, I suggest you that you buy this and try it once or wait for sometime until the full release comes (Story Mode, I'm really looking forward to that!).
My last warning ..
"Beware of the wolves, the cold, or even yourself as you play this game".

This game has been on my mind ever since I bought it, so I felt like I need to get everything out about how much I love this game and what needs to be improved. Mild spoilers, although there isn't much to spoil at all.
Also, TLDR; Feels like a Super Mario Sunshine sequel, movement is the best part, music is great, felt like it was too short and there wasn't much to do besides completing the game and getting 100%, questionable level designs, overall solid game but needs a few tweaks + more content (plz give me DLC I will give you all my money). 8/10
The Pros:
- this game is so ♥♥♥♥ing cute. 'nuff said.
- the music is very well put together. The songs are catchy and well orchastrated and fit the theme of whatever level you are on.
- speedrunning is something I love watching, but I haven't really got myself into it. This game, I would say, has actually peaked my interest in speedrunning because of the amount of options that can help you with a speedrun, such as timers, auto-skip cutscenes, etc.
- the movement is a solid 10/10. So incredibly satisfying and definitely the best part of this game. I could very easily waste a few hours doing parkour around a level on my cute little moped.
- the subtle references to pop culture and other games is an incredibly nice touch. For example, in one instance, you have to collect a few gems in a certain amount of time. If you do, a flight of stairs raises from the ground that is very similar to how it is done in SMS (Super Mario Sunshine). It even had a red X on it! (one that you could spray with FLUDD in SMS). On the same note, I'm pretty sure this game is SMS 2 with how similar it is, which is very nostalgic for me.
- the levels have so much variety and are very thematic. Each level is also extremely different from one another and sticks to that theme throughout.
- lootboxes contain really cool rewards, like appearences and mask variations. Any customisation for such a cute protagonist should be mandatory.
- on the point of lootboxes, it's always refreshing to have a game reasonably cheap and have no microtransactions. I absolutely despise the lootbox systems other games have *cough* Shadow of War *cough* and I feel like if I support games like this (which I feel genuinely care about their consumers and don't try to milk as much money out of them as possible), I am promoting this type of business practice, and I hope more publishers are like this.
- some decisions in the game, which feel minor at first, will come up again in the future. For example, giving the bird detectives your pet's name, in which your pet will be mentioned later on, or drawing on your face and have that be used as your save file picture. They're very minor details, but they are nice details nevertheless.
Unfortunately, I have a few Cons:
- a lot (nearly all of them) of the mechanics/hats in this game were very short lived. You'd use them when you first got them and then used them again once or twice in the same way with hardly any variation on how you use them. I felt like all the hats (except the dweller/fox hat, some very good puzzles with this hat) were not very well utilised and I felt like they should have had more a spotlight. For example, maybe puzzles similar to shrines in Breath of the Wild would've been good.
- this is probably due to personal preference (or maybe I'm just a wimp), but the mansion level was scary for the wrong reasons. I hate jumpscares, and the game adds this intense, loud tune whenever you aggrovate the monster. The tune appears so suddenly and is so loud that I eventually got annoyed whenever I got jumped. Couple it with the questionable AI and bad decisions the monster made (you would expect the monster to do something, and it didn't, and it ended up feeling weird), and the level was by far the worst and was so glad it was over.
- the yarn is pretty much useless to my knowledge, besides 100%ing the game and crafting hats, in which you only need one or a few. The rest are useless.
- I feel the Banjo voice badge should be default. To me, I think the voice acting is bad, but bearable. However, for those who absolutely despise it, I feel like a Banjo style voice acting route would work much better. It is nice to have full voice acting, though.
- the game was very short. 3 story based planets, 1 free-roam/story planet and a finale, plus secret levels. I felt like there should've been so much more.
- I'm a perfectionist, so I like to finish an area before I move on to the next. I felt like when I completed a level, there were so many more secrets I hadn't discovered yet. However, I only had to do one secret level (purely because I couldn't find it) to 100% the game after the final level. There is only the main story and the secret levels. I don't feel like there's anything else apart from that.
- the game just is easy. The only challenging parts for me were the purple secret levels and the boss battles. The levels felt unchallenging and puzzles are generally obvious. Would've definitely liked more challenging blue secret levels and harder/more complex puzzles
- the characters were forgettable. You'd banter with them for a few seconds at a time and after you'd completed that planet, the only time you'd see them again is at the end of the game.
Overall, I liked this game alot. I don't usually like ratings, but I'd probably give it a solid 8/10.

I'm starting to get worried that my reviews keep following the same format and eventually people will realise that the opening statement is almost always irrelevant and can be skipped without penalty.
Refunct is a game that really, really seems to want to style itself as an airport game, but never really makes it there. It's short, like irritatingly short. Not really the "oh that was cute, I'm full of warm fuzzies anyway" short, but the "I can't believe I bought Dungeons and Daemons at full price" short. The final achievement for this game is to complete it in four minutes or less.
The art style is fine, the atmosphere is fine, and full price is only three dollars, but I still like to finish a game with some semblance of knowing what I did in it, Kairo excluded, and you don't get that here. Near as I can figure, the goal is to put grass on 100% of the concrete tiles by stepping on them, and pushing red activation buttons, which will raise more tiles to have grass planted. But it's not really a puzzle game. Surely, you do have to figure out how to go about raising the next tile cluster, but you also have a massive glowing ray of light from the heavens to let your brainless finger motions complete the game on autopilot.
The parkour mechanics makes movement fun, but mechanics without much of a purpose just makes it a sandbox of sorts and doesn't really keep interest in the way that some browser games with the same mechanics have. Spending more time and adding more complexity and depth would have gone a long way for this game. My review is negative.

A Hat in Time is one of my favorite games I have played in a long time. You can tell the developers really put a lot of love into this game. Every level is different and always brings something new to the table. It does a fantastic job at keeping things fresh by giving you new abilities and introducing new mechanics at the right time. The gameplay is perfect, the controls feel tight and responsive and for the most part Hat Girl did exactly what I wanted. (I only played with a Xbox One controller) The art design is great and most of all super cute! It reminded me of Costume Quest mixed with a Nintendo game. Speaking of Nintendo games A Hat in Time is clearly inspired by games like Super Mario 64 and Banjo Kazooie which for me is a good thing because I love old school 3d platforms. You will be going back to previous levels frequently to find things you missed or couldn't access becouse you didnt have the right ability yet. The writing is good for the most part but isn't quite as good near the end. The whole ending seems a little rushed. I was able to beat it in about 10 hours and I was taking my time. I was able to 100% it in nearly 13 hours. It is not the most challenging game so if you're looking for a hard 3d platformer this definitely isn't it. It should also be noted that coop should be coming soon. As for performance I had a issue with stuttering until I forced SLI off. After that it ran impressively smooth. It's also nice to see a game explain what the graphics options actually do and there's plenty to tweak.
Pros:
- Gameplay is superb and feels great
- Writing is good for the most part
- Lots of level variety
- Good unlocking pace
- Great soundtrack
- Good performance on my machine
- Super Cute!
- No microtransactions
Cons:
- Short and left me wanting more
- Very easy
- Seems rushed towards the end
Overall this is one of the best games I have played in a long time and definitely the best current 3d platformer. I just wish there was more of it and that the ending didn't feel so rushed. If you enjoy old 3d platformers I would definitely recommend this! If you don't I would still recommend this because it is an amazing game and you can tell the developers really put a lot of passion into it. If I had to rate this I would give it a 9.5/10! Definitely worth full price!

Changed to "recommended" for anyone even slightly interested in tower defense games and cats. The best part is probably the dev's quick response to fixing the issues myself and other reviewers have had with the game, including bugs.
Since the dev has now fixed the bugs preventing me from progressing, I can now see more of the changes made since my original review (below). I have not earned my way to the different modes yet, so I'm just on the first one and my review only covers that. I'm playing in ez mode where Kingkat does not take your coins down to 500 as he did originally (and still does in the harder mode). In ez mode you get to keep whatever you earn and take as much as you want into battle. This may be OP and not challenging for many players, and those players can of course choose to play the harder mode. Since tower defense games aren't really my favorite (this is the only one I own in fact) it's a welcome casual feel for me and anyone looking for a casual but still fun experience would enjoy this, no doubt. Even with unlimited coins allowed in battle, you still can't expect to breeze through the game without earning upgrades and being tactical in your approach to defense.
Dev has also made the litterbox minigame much less annoying than it was originally. It's now much faster paced. Now too that I've been able to progress well it's not even necessary to play it since I can get a ton of coins from actual tower defense, but you do get free items from playing it and coins are always useful so it's never a pointless game, but can be avoided after a lot of progression if you desire. The Chow minigame could be avoided as well if you find yourself drowning in coins from simply chewing on dogs instead, but I find it interesting.
In case viewers opt not to read my original review below, the last part is still valid, so a repeat here: "The music is also quite catchy and the style of the game is fitting for what it seems like it's trying to be, not really sure how to describe the style though without coming off as though I don't like it. I'm neutral on that stance if anything, it's in no way bad."
The only issue I see now is that there doesn't appear to be a way to swap modes, so once you choose ez or hard you're stuck with it. Will suggest that among a couple other things in a post on the forums, otherwise I feel it's solid from what I've seen so far.

*ORIGINAL REVIEW*
I suppose I should start with the disclaimer that I'm not usually a fan of tower defense games. This is in fact the only one I own. Unfortunately, this is much less a tower defense and more a litter box cleaning simulator. Yes, you can earn coins by other means, but here's the main problems with those means:
1. The "chow" mini game (where you feed cats for coins and to be able to earn them for free use during battle) can only be played once and only if you progressed during your last run. I've not been able to play it after 3 runs now, I assume that's because each time I only managed to make it to wave 10 each time, never beating my highest score.
2. If you have more than 500 coins before entering battle, Kingkat takes all of your excess coins from you. He does NOT return them afterwards. If you're stuck like I am, this really sucks because that means you can't actually gain any coins simply by battling, you absolutely must play the litter box mini game and ONLY the litter box mini game to earn upgrades.
Now, this would be fine if the litterbox mini game was not tedious and irritating... but it is. Grab one poo, another appears, sometimes multiple. The small ones are worth 60, large worth 100, and it takes a bit of time to sift them, so it's not instant pick up. There's also the little waves of urine odor which can be dealt with with a spray that you earn through the litterbox mini game, but they also vanish over time if you just leave them. If you do manage to clear out the whole litter box you get a rain of money until something appears again. It's quite difficult to keep the box cleared though, so you sit there having to poke at it for quite a while before being able to upgrade anything.
If the dev reads this at all, I would ask you to consider either changing the way the litterbox minigame works (make it less tedious or make cleaning it more worth while) or add other means of making money, maybe more mini games or make battling more worthwhile (no more greedy Kingkats maybe). If any of that gets changed I will gladly revisit the game and consider changing my review to "recommended" instead of not.
If you can get past the tediousness of the upgrades system, the tower defense part is pretty fun from what I've been able to see so far. The music is also quite catchy and the style of the game is fitting for what it seems like it's trying to be, not really sure how to describe the style though without coming off as though I don't like it. I'm neutral on that stance if anything, it's in no way bad.

Banished is a game that throws you right into the middle of fight for survival. However, this fight isn't your typical fight. Its a fight against the elements.
From the start you're given a few families with barely anything, and you're tasked to shelter, provide, and watch over your exiles. In the begining you have enough resources to take care of their immediate concerns, but those resources soon run out. With winter fast approaching your concern for lumber and food rises. You begin asking yourself is there enough food; is there enough fuel; are there enough houses availabel? Just as Autumn passes and winter satrts knocking at your door, you are tasked with putting the fate of your village on the line. As the winter rages on and food and fuel dwindle down you find yourself nervous. And as winter peaks with your margin narrowly positive you realize that everything has worked out. With your first winter done you can now enjoy the game, until next winter that is...
Overall I find the game to be a very relaxing and pleasent game. It requires a good amount of thinking, but it's not to much to enjoy the game. Its very simple and has great mechanics. Just when you think the game is getting old the mods (via steam and other sites) really help to get you back into it, and the community for the game is great as well.

The Long Dark pulls no punches and gives no handouts. It is a game that will chill you to the core and freeze you to the bone. Once you enter this snowy expanse of woods, you will turn on survival mode. You will become the character you control. Your stomach will grumble when your character is hungry. You will shiver when your character is cold.
Best of all - you will jump for joy the first time you find a gun. A gun in this game is a new house, new clothes, and a new way of life. But don't take it for granted -- you will still die.
I recommend The Long Dark for anyone and everyone. This game is unique, immersive, and best of all, fun. You literally FEEL the fear that your character portrays when his/her heart starts thumping after spotting a wolf that's a little too close for comfort. You will be chilled, thrilled, and killed in this survival game.
Buy it.
Buy it now and don't question whether you should buy it or not. You will be happy that you did.

Aight so some info on gameplay mechanics: You have humans and seraphs, humans are melee fighters, seraphs are all magic users of 1 element. The main mechanics of the battle system in this game is being able to swap seraph around in battle and the armitization mechanic which fuses a seraph and human together into one unit that fights with that element of that seraph. You also do not have TP but instead you have a bar of SC that recharges when defending or doing nothing (moving counts as something). In a sense, its nice that SC recharges very easily in combat from just defending and grazing attacks (dodging attacks at the last moment). However this limits you from long combos forcing you to wait for your SC bar to recharge, which takes about 1-2 seconds from an empty bar which normally wouldn't be an issue.... But the AI in this game is utter garbage it makes all boss fights into you just pummeling the boss alone while your teammates are dead or set to defend where all they do is heal and get hit by attacks since they don't know how to guard. The absolute worst is when the bosses start to rush down your AI teammates instead of you so you are trying your damnest to keep your team alive but they just stand there drooling or casting a heal as the boss pummels their face in. I've tried everything to manipulate the AI. I would spam attack and defend nonstop to have them attack then back off when i knew the boss would become immune to damage (from being combo'd too long) but even then, they would take their time switching between attack and defense it was too easy for a boss to kill them.
On another note, the dungeons are poor quality as well. There aren't really any puzzles just "press elemtnal button to open special elemental door\mechanic that happens to be in your way". Otherwise its just trekking through ruins and picking up chests if you want take the time to get them.
I enjoyed the story, I enjoyed the battle mechanics, I enjoyed the characters for the most part. AI being a liability makes it a chore to play on harder difficulties but if you can do co-op local its fun then. It was worth my $20 at least. It just sucks having to solo boss fights.

I have taken sometime to play this game myself and I decided that I should write a review here so that it would be helpful for those who read it and decide whether to purchase this game or not.
Get to the point, right now the game is in 'Early Access' so it is not really complete. However, personally, only what the Early Access has offered now worths the money.
The very first thing that can be accounted as pros is the the game's very own concept. It is a new dimension of 'survival game', unlike many mainstream survival game lists which involve zombies and mutants to horrify you, this game is another story: just you against the 'Mother Nature'. You are on your own, among the cold, hunger, thirst, tiredness, or even danger from wolves. All you need to do is 'survive'. It sounds simple and uninteresting, but believe me this game is well enough even with this simplicity in this game genre. No safe place with lots of supplies (unless you choose 'Pilgrim' mode). You need to take risks with your own actions. Everything is by yourself.
The gameplay ... I don't know if I should classify it as a pro or con, but it is mixed. You can never expect anything from each playthrough; when you restart, everything except the regions will be resetted. This gives you the survival experience to some extends. For example, you might find a rifle, the only 'real' weapon in the game, without any bullets before you find one bullet miles away, or you need a can opener but still yet to be found; what will you do? which way? where is it going to be? Everything which other survival games may overlook matters in this game. You need clothes to keep you warm, raw food, if not cooked well, can be a threat when eaten, or you can even hurt your legs if you do not watch your steps (which happens to me a lot lol). These are some of the situations that I found and I need to give the 'thumb up' for the developer's careful planning so as to make this game as realistc as possible.
However, there is something that still bugs me; the wolves. They still lack realistic movements: too repetitive and can be easy to deal with as you get get used to the game. Even though the developer has mentioned something about the wolves, their movements and some behaviors, such as how slow or fast it should be in different situations, are needed for consideration *for developers*. I hope if the wolves are readjusted in the right way it would gives me more exciting experience. Nevertheless, even with this comment I still find dealing with wolves sometimes hard anyway. (I heard that more wildlife will be added, so it might be the solution for this problem as well.)
If you are fans of survival game and need a new dimension on survival experience, I suggest you that you buy this and try it once or wait for sometime until the full release comes (Story Mode, I'm really looking forward to that!).
My last warning ..
"Beware of the wolves, the cold, or even yourself as you play this game".

This game is a terribly good game. I got it on sale for a good price and I am happy with what I payed for it.  My brother (who loves horror movies but can't stand playing horror games) wanted me to play this game so he could watch.
It is a first-person survival horror game.  You don't actually fight anyone, you just have to run and hide.  I thoroughly enjoyed the story, so much so that I picked up the DLC Whistleblower for it (which I am still yet to finish).  If you like horror games then you will most likely love this game.  As difficult as it was for me, I was able to finish the main story (which I am quite proud of!).  It can be a little bit repetative at times; you will be sent to find something or to fix something and each time you are in a dimly lit locale running and hiding from some disfigured, psychologically disturbed manianc trying to kill you.  Admittedly, at one point I got scared so good that I jumped and through my mouse across the room, resulting in me not being able to escape and obviously being hacked to bits.
I was playing on my ASUS G46 Gaming Laptop hooked up to a TV via HDMI cable.  Everything ran smoothly on the highest settings and the graphics were easy on the eyes, so to speak.
All-in-all, if you like survival horror games or if you're looking for a challenge you will enjoy this game.  Be prepared to run, hide, and most likely scream.

Just finished my first playthrough, all sidequests and dungeons done with 35 hours of playtime, albeit 1 or 2 hours of idling. Absolutely beautiful game. After the first couple of hours the main character goes from a bland insert to the defined protagonist who has morals and a personality.
PROS
*I love all the characters, and could totally watch an anime of something like this.
*The combat is probably the best thing about this game. Though my personal favorite thing is how cinematics are done. Most cutscenes are in engine, and look pretty decent. But rather than go the Final Fantasy route of putting CGI cutscenes in, they decided to make the major cutscenes in an anime style. All of these cutscenes are always just badass and fun to watch in general.
*Exploration is fun and rewarding
*TONS of optional stuff. Extra dungeons, solo challenges, side quests, mini bosses that can be found in a general area or dungeon.
*Character Customization actually stays with you in cutscenes (it's the little things)
*Absolutely love the music. There's a free God Eater DLC that changes the battle music, and that sounds good too. It's all really great adventure music. Every so often there's a dungeon theme that I don't like though.
*Speaking out of the 4th wall, this is a great PC port. Never had any issues, controller was detected right off the bat, It not only picked a perfect resolution that I kept a solid 30 frames at the entire way through, but it displayed on my 4k TV will no trouble or configuration really needed.
CONS
* The dungeons, good lord. They just reskin textures for every dungeon ; always a winding hall, always a door you have to punch, always things falling from the ceilings. Even some of the trials (think temples from Zelda) are repetitive and tedious when it comes to navigation. Luckly the combat is still fun enough to keep me from getting bored.
* The first few hours. If the first five hours of this game were the whole playthrough, i'd probably give this game a 5. Sooo boring, Christ. The characters don't evolve at all until at least the first dungeon, or when you have all 4 seraphs. But when it gets going, it gets going. Lilah makes word puns, Edna pisses off Mikleo, Mikleo makes smart remarks to Sorey, etc.
*Alisha being written off early. Basically in the first few hours of the game, you get a human partner named Alisha. Soon, she has duties to see to, and leaves, then you get a new companion. Alisha pops up a few more times, but she's never a character that can fight with you again, ever. I feel that they took her out just to package her side of the story as DLC, and that... that really sucks.

Freebie is a "casual game" where you throw projectiles, according to speed, direction, and velocity, against a spinning paddle, in order to hit the green corners/walls/surface and avoid the red ones.
Freebie does not contain any tutorial/explanation on how the game works with the exception of the controls menu.
The name of the game, Freebie, has no relation to the game itself or the price of its content and may be a reference to its developers, the Free Games Info Team.
The game contains 5 achievements, being the hardest one reach 50 points, and contains a leaderboard, which is easily, and constantly hacked.
During the gameplay, you will find +1 point and +1 life, which you can get them by hitting them with the projectile.
The Gameplay does a great job on the balance between +1 life or point, yet, it fails on not letting the player have more than 5 lives.
This Game supports Xbox 360 controller, yet, the balance between controller and keyboard is not consistent.
The controller supports taking screenshots during the game, while on the keyboard, it's not possible to do it.
On the keyboard, you can shoot by clicking on the cubes, or by using the arrows, which you will only use 2 of them, even though the controls' section shows all arrows keys.
This game contains the main menu and the gameplay.
The main menu is blanket and it's full of buttons, making it distracting and very painful to understand/navigate it.
The gameplay itself contains two theme modes: Classic Theme and Epilepsy Theme; which both are the same except the background during the gameplay. Does not contain any flashing lights, only flashing colors.
The game contains three tracks and sound effects.
The only sound effect that exists it's when the projectile is fired, this cannot be muted, in contrary to the soundtrack.
The developer made this game with such low content, making it look as a low-budget-quick-arcade-game for quick cash, and shows no intention to keep trying to fix the Leaderboard/Bugs/Crashes and/or improve the game.
Freebie is not a "game", it's an arcade game that doesn't have the support necessary, from content, and from the developer to keep the player and game "alive". It shouldn't cost any price and shouldn't be considered as a game.

I was going to recommend this game, because for about 60% of this game the story is bearable but idiotic.
The beginning is great, atmospheric, and tense. The diner is also the most developed area in the entire game.
It never reaches that height again, with Fahrenheit it's always a downward slope. You thought you'd seen the dumbest possible thing in a video game, and then it pulls the rug out from under you and it gets even more idiotic.
Nothing you do matters, there's only three or four endings, and plot points are introduced and promptly forgotten as soon as possible.
It starts off looking like a really interesting investigation thriller, and then descends into madness until you have become the leader of a hobo uprising against the mayan illuminati and a sentient free-floating AI cyborg that just materialized out of thin air. Then you drive out to New Mexico ((from New York)) in a Snow Cat, kill both primary antagonists without a scratch, and go home. Everything goes back to Status Quo with the only difference being that Lucas and his Ex are dead except Lucas isn't dead and Carla is pregnant with the next Avatar-- err... Chroma master?
David Cage constantly strokes his ego throughout the game and steals wholesale from popular media (such as the Matrix, Star Wars, Indiana Jones, Silent Hill, etc). The main McGuffin is a little girl who they forgot to hire a voice actor for.
The characters are mostly pretty flat (the most likable ones are the two CSI guys, Mario and Luigi). Tyler, one of two black characters in the entire game, is a complete stereotype, and is constantly breaking the fourth wall. By the way, he is also completely despicable and useless.
Lucas is a Gary Stu who has unexplained powers with arbitrary rules. Apparently he's like 80 years old because he was a kid in the 1930s. He dies at some point, but is revived by the robot through some kind of magic that is never explained. He falls in love with Carla and he impregnates her as a zombie with a -47 C body temperature ((thus he would be sterile...)).
Carla is annoying and useless. All the girl characters seem to exist exclusively to take their clothes off.
At first all of this is hilarious and laughable and so unbelievably stupid. Eventually, due in part to annoying 'gameplay' sections (Metal Gear Solid with babby Lucas, the evidence room, endless QTE), and the constantly spiralling plot and quality it just becomes unbearable. It's impossible to follow, and by the time SANTA MONICAAAAA started playing in the credits I had become a gibbering inconsolable mess of confusion and boredom.
There is no gameplay in the entire game-- which isn't necessarilly a bad thing, except what's there are tedious and disengagingly easy Simon Says quick time events that break immersion and ruin the atmosphere always.
Some notable sequences:
-JOHNNNNN
-BUGS
-AHHH SERVER ISSUE
-MY HOUSE IS TRYING TO KILL ME
-CARS?!
-TAKE THAT COPPERS
-GOKU POWERS GO
-ANGEL STATUE ATTACK
-WHERE'S THE FAT KID
-TRY NOT TO DROWN
-BALANCING ACT?!
-AHHHHHH
-DRAGON BALL C*
-BIRDS
-????????????????
There's like four or five tracks in the OST, and the rest is garbage licensed music. Sound design gets really skimped out on later in the game.
Graphically, it's fine. The team that worked on the Mocap and most of the animation was clearly very talented-- it looks great for when it came out. In the last act even this falls apart, and everything starts to look like a crappy GMod Machinima. About 50% of the way through, every level becomes underdeveloped and totally empty.
The most entertaining part of the game was trying to find every stupid bonus card and then watching the insane bonus videos-- and turning on SANTAA MOOONIICCAAA

When I was about 14 years old, I owned this game on PS2, but I could never beat it back then. Nowadays I understand why that was: the gameplay just sucks.
Though I'm intrigued by the story and think that the game is quite atmospheric, it ultimately is ruined by design flaws and horrible controls.
The most terrible feature of this game are the quick time events, as many players lament. They appear far too often and distract from what is happening in the game, because firstly the time to respond to the prompts is very short and secondly the prompts, designed as two 'Simon says'-like games, each corresponding with one of the analog sticks (when you play with a controller, obviously), cover a large portion of the screen and thus you kinda miss what is happening while you hastily try to succeed at these dull minigames. While I'm at it, the QTE sequences sometimes span over 3-4 minutes. I didn't time it exactly, but let me assure you, they're going on longer than they should.
Some of the other aforementioned design flaws include:
- Dialogue options are described too vaguely and, again, the time to respond is just too short. I never really had time to decide for a specific dialogue option.
- Almost all actual gameplay passages overstay their welcome, like the part with
- Concerning the controls, there was a minigame in which you shoot targets at a gun range from a first person perspective and you actually aim with the frickin left stick, disregarding the industry standard completely. That one really bugged me. (Didn't actually check, whether this could be changed in the options, but I doubt it)
Aside from that, I found the game to be a little glitchy now and again, nothing game breaking, but just ugly to look at.
On a positive note, I really liked the score and most of the voice acting. The story so far was also not bad, nothing fancy either, but above the videogame average, I'd say.
But ultimately the game annoyed the hell out of me and I couldn't finish it. I can appreciate what David Cage was trying to do and actually am thankful this game existed, since it led to Heavy Rain and Beyond, which were way more pleasant experiences for me.

Okay, let me start out by saying I don't hate this game. Really, I don't, I think it's interesting and realistic (if you put the disasters on or forget to place a building that provides food within the first week or firewood before the winter... oops...), and I genuinely think there is potential here. Yet there is one thing this game lacks, and that is purpose.
There are no goals to make you play the game, you're just making a small settlement grow into its own goddamn country. And I know what you might be thinking: "This game has achievements, though, shouldn't that be able to tide you over?". I see that, and yes, logically this should tide me over. If there wasn't some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t bottleneck-thing going on. Look at all the hours I put into this. Hours and hours trying to get even one achievement, and over half of that is after I found out which of them is most likely to be the only one that I can get at this point. My problem is either that the village has expanded too much or too little. Either I have too many people or too few workers. If this bottleneck-achievement-getting wasn't an issue, I'd probably say "Oh well, it had problems, but at least we got something to try doing. After all, everybody loves them some achievements", but as is, the game gives you no purpose to continue playing.
This might be an idiotic line of thinking (since the achievements are often put in after the game's release), but if you have no purpose (other than to finish the tutorial of course) in the first place, and the outside influence whose entire purpose is giving you more reasons to play the game are bottlenecked to the point where you're almost forcing yourself to play, just to see if you can't meet that one goal just once, the game becomes almost like a chore rather than a game (which is a deadly game sin, I am sure). (Oh, and if you're still unsure as to the legitimacy of using achievements as a reason to not get a game, the achievements are actually implemented into the game itself. I♥♥♥♥♥♥you not, they even have their own tab on the menu. Either my computer does some black magic behind my back, or the bottleneck is real, goddamnit.)
So if you're looking to just build a city, go ahead. I, for one, can't recommend a game that feels empty and meaningless.
If you want a game that actually does both purpose and city-building better, check out "Black and White 2". It has a plot,  you get to be a god (which, by the way, means some people will worship you without questioning your... *ahem* questionable activities...), and you get to have a pet WOLF OR LION (or cow or monkey, but they're not as much fun... Okay the cow is, the monkey isn't... Because holy cow...) that have some kick♥♥♥♥♥AI (you can teach them to weightlift rocks, poop on villagers, and DESTROY ALL OF YOUR ENEMIES BEFORE YOUR CITY GATES). It's probably not on steam today, but one beautiful day it might be.

Having just completed this game, I can honestly say that it is probably my favorite game of this year. It's really nostalgic, bringing to mind old action/platformer/collect-a-thon games like Banjo-Kazooie or Spyro. Even more so, this game is fun. It's far too rare these days to find games designed purely for fun. I spent time just exploring all of the worlds because there were so many ways to get around that it was consistently enjoyable.
Granted, I did notice a few flaws. For starters, the camera is really intrusive at times. It either zooms too far into the character that you cannot be aware of hazards, or it gets stuck on walls and jolts which makes you lose your sense of direction. This makes platforming incredibly difficult when it occurs, but thankfully that isn't too often. Speaking of platforming, there was one other issue I noticed whilst platforming. This may just be me, as I haven't read any other reviews mentioning it. There were instances when I had trouble performing jumps because the camera wasn't really displaying any sense of depth. I would think I was dead-centered on a platform and realize far too late that I had drastically over-shot it. I checked this on multiple graphics settings, and didn't really notice any change. Again, this may have just been me.
One other minor grievance is that the game is a little short. If you just play through the chapters without getting any bonuses save for the hats, this game could feasibly be finished in as little as 5 hours, perhaps less. Granted, what is here is great. I just wish there were a little more.
That all being said, I absolutely adore this game. No matter what I was doing while playing, I was having fun.

With this brutal realism you'll quickly finding yourself seeking shelter from all forms of enemy fire, as your character feels the effects of suppression and fatigue. All this detail leads to great multiplayer experience. Although only for people looking for realism and tactics over kill streaks and care packages.

Just finished my first playthrough, all sidequests and dungeons done with 35 hours of playtime, albeit 1 or 2 hours of idling. Absolutely beautiful game. After the first couple of hours the main character goes from a bland insert to the defined protagonist who has morals and a personality.
PROS
*I love all the characters, and could totally watch an anime of something like this.
*The combat is probably the best thing about this game. Though my personal favorite thing is how cinematics are done. Most cutscenes are in engine, and look pretty decent. But rather than go the Final Fantasy route of putting CGI cutscenes in, they decided to make the major cutscenes in an anime style. All of these cutscenes are always just badass and fun to watch in general.
*Exploration is fun and rewarding
*TONS of optional stuff. Extra dungeons, solo challenges, side quests, mini bosses that can be found in a general area or dungeon.
*Character Customization actually stays with you in cutscenes (it's the little things)
*Absolutely love the music. There's a free God Eater DLC that changes the battle music, and that sounds good too. It's all really great adventure music. Every so often there's a dungeon theme that I don't like though.
*Speaking out of the 4th wall, this is a great PC port. Never had any issues, controller was detected right off the bat, It not only picked a perfect resolution that I kept a solid 30 frames at the entire way through, but it displayed on my 4k TV will no trouble or configuration really needed.
CONS
* The dungeons, good lord. They just reskin textures for every dungeon ; always a winding hall, always a door you have to punch, always things falling from the ceilings. Even some of the trials (think temples from Zelda) are repetitive and tedious when it comes to navigation. Luckly the combat is still fun enough to keep me from getting bored.
* The first few hours. If the first five hours of this game were the whole playthrough, i'd probably give this game a 5. Sooo boring, Christ. The characters don't evolve at all until at least the first dungeon, or when you have all 4 seraphs. But when it gets going, it gets going. Lilah makes word puns, Edna pisses off Mikleo, Mikleo makes smart remarks to Sorey, etc.
*Alisha being written off early. Basically in the first few hours of the game, you get a human partner named Alisha. Soon, she has duties to see to, and leaves, then you get a new companion. Alisha pops up a few more times, but she's never a character that can fight with you again, ever. I feel that they took her out just to package her side of the story as DLC, and that... that really sucks.
Great RPG. Just a really, really solid game in general. The ending is just so awesome and bittersweet and I loved every minute of it. (Exept the first couple hundred).
It's easily a high 7, low 8 for me. Beautiful game.

I've only just started to play this game and get the hang of it--and thankfully I'm not regretting my purchase. This game is a  true survival game--one man (or woman) pitted against the elements in a variety of ways. Dangers lurk around every corner; wolves, starvation, hypothermia, blood loss, and sepsis are all very real threats in this game. And after just 3 "days" of survival, you'll never be more thankful to come across a granola bar in your life. I really enjoy what this game offers so far, and hope that the devs continue to expand upon this game greatly. I would like to see some method of expanding the inventory pack, or at least scaling down existing inventory (my "clothes" should not weigh 13+ lbs)... I would like to see a sleigh to carry supplies in. Make it penalizing, such as spiking fatigue and draining calories to move... but at least allow for portability. I would also like to see more maps with greater variety. And most importantly, I would like to see more offensive weaponry. It is far too unrealistically difficult to come across a gun, or a hatchet. Or even a knife. Everyone has knives. And I should be able to practice throwing it. At wolves.
At any rate, I highly recommend this game. For the price, you really can't go wrong.

It's not Tales of the Abyss or Vesperia in terms of characters and story but it's still a great game. A bit misundertood if anything else but what game in a long franchise isn't? I haven't played Xillia or Graces but this is the first game in the series where the combat already starts off fun with you being able to do full fledged combos. The removal traditional MP (or TP in this series' case) took some getting used to but I enjoyed it a lot once I did. Perfecting combos cancels and managing your meter to get quick refills to continue said combo. Much less of a spam fest this way. Feels like a fighting game more than anything else. I never had a huge issue with the camera except for during co-op play but that's more so due to the fact that battles are seamless now.
Party system is one of the few things I don't like. You can only have two humans. You can't have Sorey and 3 other Seraphim. Sorey and the other character sort of have their own teammate and they can switch out the Seraphim they want, at will. This limits party variety in my honest opinion. Being able to switch on the fly is fun and handy though.
You no longer have the basic level up, get skill, equip gear, rinse repeat. How strong you are is determined by your skills and equipment. Matching up certain skills will give you large or small stat bonus depending on what you match. I don't really have a problem with the system and it never felt like a grind because I never had to go out of my way. Or at least never felt like I had to. At least the system is different, I will give it that. Whether you like it or not is up to you.
Speaking of gear. There is a fairly in depth crafting system but I haven't really gotten too far into it. It never felt entirely necessary.
Storywise the game is pretty standard although it does have the typical major twists that all Tales games have. And these you actually don't see coming from a mile away! (Okay well maybe two). Despite being standard and never going in depth, the characters are still very likable with each having their own distinct personalities. I think the overall story is a callback to old school JRPGs. Naive, sheltered young man discovers what the world is really like and his destiny in said world. It makes since as this was an anniversary game if I'm not mistaken. It's nothing we haven't seen before but it's still nice to see such a determined protag. Sorey is basically anime Jesus. The game does however go to some really dark places though which contrast the light tone the game has at times. Skits are hilarious, per usual.
Many people complain about the dungeons  in this but I honestly never thought they were good in any of the Tales games except for maybe Abyss. They always felt like pointless filler. Same with the open worlds. It's basically the same here but now the open world is more akin to something like Skyrim, albeit with far less stuff. It's still a step in the right direction in my honest opinion.
Graphics and sountrack are absolutely amazing in this game. Colors pop and the score just brings everything to life. Probably my favorite overall soundtrack in the series that I've played. If you can run this at 4k, I highly recommend it. In terms of voice acting, I only listen to Japanese because that's my preference these days but regardless the characters voices fit the personality.
Like all Tales games the main story is 40+ hours and you have much more content with side quests and New Game+ and just grinding. Getting all yours skills. Getting the best gear. Finding all the skits. Doing every single side objective.
If you're a fan of Tales or JRPGS in general, I would definitely recommend this. It's not the best Tales game ever made but it's certainly not the worst. Not even close. This game shows a lot of promise and makes me hopeful for a series I lost interest in after Vesperia. If you're a hardcore fan who dislikes any sort of change to the formula, stay away. Or lack there of in some cases. ;)

I can't suggest this program enough! I even suggest it over the newer RPG Maker MV! If you want something simple to play around with, or a way to make a more serious commerical project without having to learn all the complicated parts of game development, you can find no better program. Not to mention, it's incredibly affordable, espically when it's on sell!
The community revolving around it is great as well, and plenty of people offer their created resources to you for free even in the commerical game projects. Just make sure you give them proper credit and make sure it is actually okay.
It's very easy to learn as you go, just search any issue you have on the internet and you can likely find a way to solve it.
I have been using this program to produce an indie RPG game single handedly the past year or so, and it's worked very nicely. I am still a ways out from being complete, but that is because of the scope of my project. A simple project could be completed quite quickly.
And if you are put off my turn-based games, scripts even exist to make the combat closer to old Zelda games!
All around, it's just very versatile, powerful, professional, and cheap.
The only problem is, if you don't try hard enough, your game will come out very generic. :(

Physics and art - what can go wrong? As it appears, a lot: the game runs in 1024x768, but not stretched, it does a fake fullscreen by adding huge black borders. (You can make it windowed by pressing Esc, that's not in the settings menu.) The microphone input cannot be calibrated to a "rest" sound, as a result my balloon always went up into the sky. With voice input active, the game crashes a lot, too. Which means I had to play it with mouse and space bar.
And you need a lot of patience: in the first 6 levels, the main game mechanic means you stay at one height to get up to speed and then quickly rise into a countercurrent to hop over an obstacle. Get the timing on this even slightly wrong, and you may need to do it again.. and again... and again. Add random annoying spikey bits that often don't even look spikey for extra aggravation, and borders you can easily fly out of in any direction to restart the level for that extra patience drain.
I'm tired now and don't have the patience, and that's why didn't complete it and don't recommend it. Your mileage may vary.

SUPERHOT is the first person shooter where time moves only when you move. It's a new take on fps formula and it is damn refreshing and unique. It bears many similarities with Hotline Miami (the first), you can die fast and respawn fast and it's basically a puzzle game where you think of creative ways to stay alive while others don't.
The story is rather barebone, you basically do a series of semi connected missions with some filler text in between. It's a little bit twisted but nowhere near the Hotline Miami's story. There are additional unlockable modes. Endless, where you just kill stuff until you're killed. Challenge, where you have to get through 25 levels with set conditions, ie. katana only. Two time attack modes, one where clock stops when you stop and the other where clock doesn't stop.
The story mode alone took me 2.5 hrs and it was innovative and fun. The challenges are fun and should take a while. And then there's endless. And time attack. And maybe challenges again! The content is there, and it's fun, but it's also a bit on the expensive side. I'd say for 15 euro this should be an insta buy, but for over 20 it's a bit expensive. I was a kickstarter backer, so well...
I liked:
* almost everything!
* innovative mechanics
* unique gameplay
* solid presentation
I disliked:
* the "super hot" repeated over and over again after each level was super annoying
Get this:
* if you're looking for something original
* if you liked Hotline Miami
Don't get this:
* if you're looking for a standard fps
* if you're not into puzzle murdering

Yep, I've waited a long time to be able to review this, and now, here it is.
I would reccomend this to anyone who wants the spooky/paranoia experience without the blood and gore that you see in stuff like Neverending Nightmares. While blood is acceptable and expected, it isn't something you can have around slightly younger audiences (Not toddlers, but 4th grade through middle school.)
However, this game is NOT, I repeat, NOT for everyone.
It all depends on how you look at horror games.
If you start this game up expecting another Amnesia or Slender type get-chased-by-monster game, then you WILL BE DISAPPOINTED. This game is NOTHING LIKE THEM. In this game, you play as the night guard for a run-down soon-to-close pizzeria with animatronic animals that come to life at night and try to kill you. Think of it as if Chuck E. Cheese and Night at the museum had a baby raised by Satan.
In FNaF, you cannot run. No, you aren't running around the Pizzeria trying to not get caught from 12 to 6. You work form a tiny office with 5 ways to interact: Close 2 doors, Turn on 2 lights, and check the various cameras to track Freddy and Co. throughout the building.
To sub-quote the mighty BrutalMoose "Essentially you are in the center of a giant Pac-Man maze trying to keep the robots out."
This game relies on the creepiness of it's environment as opposed to being scared of Freddy himself. And it does that well. This game changes everything you know about horror games and twists it, and you may or may not love it. It also may or may not be worth the 5 american bucks you spent on it. Fortunately there's a mobile version that's cheaper.

Okay, let me start out by saying I don't hate this game. Really, I don't, I think it's interesting and realistic (if you put the disasters on or forget to place a building that provides food within the first week or firewood before the winter... oops...), and I genuinely think there is potential here. Yet there is one thing this game lacks, and that is purpose.
There are no goals to make you play the game, you're just making a small settlement grow into its own goddamn country. And I know what you might be thinking: "This game has achievements, though, shouldn't that be able to tide you over?". I see that, and yes, logically this should tide me over. If there wasn't some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t bottleneck-thing going on. Look at all the hours I put into this. Hours and hours trying to get even one achievement, and over half of that is after I found out which of them is most likely to be the only one that I can get at this point. My problem is either that the village has expanded too much or too little. Either I have too many people or too few workers. If this bottleneck-achievement-getting wasn't an issue, I'd probably say "Oh well, it had problems, but at least we got something to try doing. After all, everybody loves them some achievements", but as is, the game gives you no purpose to continue playing.
This might be an idiotic line of thinking (since the achievements are often put in after the game's release), but if you have no purpose (other than to finish the tutorial of course) in the first place, and the outside influence whose entire purpose is giving you more reasons to play the game are bottlenecked to the point where you're almost forcing yourself to play, just to see if you can't meet that one goal just once, the game becomes almost like a chore rather than a game (which is a deadly game sin, I am sure). (Oh, and if you're still unsure as to the legitimacy of using achievements as a reason to not get a game, the achievements are actually implemented into the game itself. I♥♥♥♥♥♥you not, they even have their own tab on the menu. Either my computer does some black magic behind my back, or the bottleneck is real, goddamnit.)
So if you're looking to just build a city, go ahead. I, for one, can't recommend a game that feels empty and meaningless.
If you want a game that actually does both purpose and city-building better, check out "Black and White 2". It has a plot,  you get to be a god (which, by the way, means some people will worship you without questioning your... *ahem* questionable activities...), and you get to have a pet WOLF OR LION (or cow or monkey, but they're not as much fun... Okay the cow is, the monkey isn't... Because holy cow...) that have some kick♥♥♥♥♥AI (you can teach them to weightlift rocks, poop on villagers, and DESTROY ALL OF YOUR ENEMIES BEFORE YOUR CITY GATES). It's probably not on steam today, but one beautiful day it might be.

It's a strange game, really. To me, it collides beatifulness of sights, marvels of almost supernatural flights, and uglyness of c.i.a. operative agenda. For sandbox game, it looks almost perfect.
But I'll start from bad side.
Story are weak, alike with any subsequent missions of "Just cause", and it's because of game pattern - CIA operative wreaking havoc and destruction on peaceful countryside for USA profit and domination. That's a little more complicated than muscling drug deals, car thefts and bank robbing, like usual gta-like stuff, don't you think? Ok, there was "Mercenaries" and brilliant "the Saboteur", and I liked them! But in those games you were aiming primarily to military objects, and were penalized for civilian casulties. Conscience sleeps well on that. But as for "just case", you blowing power and water supplies in cities and villages. You are coherently destroing all of life-suppoting communications in country for such irrelevant aim as "chaos". Oh, and for drug deals - which CIA operative ever don't get envolved in that? Worse than that is only agenda of "Prototype" game, where civilians are just food, and only thing protagonist cares about is himself. But enough of that.

I really wish there was an option inbetween good and bad on Steam, because that's what Indigo Prophecy deserves.
Starting off on a fairly shallow point, the game does not look good. It's aged pretty poorly. The animations are clunky and awkward, the character models are blocky and robotic (kinda like the original Sims). The environments actually look a bit better, but are still pretty rough. Along with visuals comes audio though, and I love this game's soundtrack. Take your time and listen to the music as you play, it's pretty great (especially when you play as Tyler and move on into Funkytown)
Let's move on from that though, onto what you're really going to be interested in with a game like this- the story (this review is pretty much spoiler free). I think it can be divided into 2 main parts. The beginning, everything is very mysterious, VERY interesting, and VERY intriguing. It very much does draw you in and makes you want to discover more. You have interesting characters, a great paranormal murder mystery, just very great stuff. But then, around halfway through the game, you start actually discovering the truth of things and, in my opinion, it goes MASSIVELY downhill. Without giving specifics, everything gets so ridiculous and over the top and goofy. It feels like you go from this interesting tense murder mystery to some campy, wacky anime series, and I find the rapid change in tone very off-putting. Maybe this comes down to personal preference, I like more of a tense kinda gritty story, if you like things getting weird and over the top you could enjoy the second half MORE. I just wish they could have chosen ONE of these themes and not switched between them halfway through the game.
Gameplay wise, it's pretty much what you expect, it's an interactive story. You walk around, make some dialogue choices, throw in some quick time events, and there ya go. You'll often find yourself doing everyday tasks like getting a drink or using the bathroom or playing with a yo-yo. Personally I found these little things fun and not trivial. One really cool thing is that you do play as 3 different main characters, each kind of with their own tone and general settings. You can more or less choose in what order you play as them, which I very much like. One very unique gameplay aspect of this game is the Sanity Meter. Throughout the story, small interactions can affect your sanity. Things like finding a clue or a positive dialogue interaction can raise your sanity (even small things like drinking a cup of coffee), and things like a major sad event or ♥♥♥♥ing up a sequence can lower it. Go too low and you'll get a Game Over where your character will go insane or commit suicide. It's a fun little system, i've played this game about 3 times and have never had a character go too low.
There is one aspect of the gameplay which I find insufferable- the Quick Time Events. Normally I dont mind these, in fact I think in a lot of games they're kinda fun. Indigo Prophecy's quick time events are not fun in any sense of the word. You really only use the analogue sticks. Two Simon-like circles appear in the middle of the screen. A direction lights up (so for example, the top part of the left circle) and you move your analogue stick in that way (so youd move your left stick up). It's simple and usually pretty easy, but the thing is they go on for WAAAAAYYYYY too long. It's mind numbing how long some of them are, and it's not even like you can actually really watch the action on the screen unfold since you have to keep your eyes on the two spheres at all times. It's. So. Boring. It's not fun at all. There's a REALLY UNGODLY long one near the end, and if you mess up on it you have to do it all over again and I swear its like 20 minutes long and on this recent playthrough it honestly made me just stop playing and give up. That's how insufferably dumb it is.
There are also a few flashback segments as well, and they're always a huge pain in the♥♥♥♥♥and not very fun. They mostly revolve around stealth, which I mean I can give them credit for inan attempt to change up the gameplay a bit, but like I said, they're usually just a pain.
Overall, I DO recommend you play Indigo Prophecy, just be warned it's very flawwed. If you enjoy Heavy Rain, it's a must-play of course. Fans of interactive stories definitely need to play this, as I feel it really kind of paved the way for a lot of the genre today.

is a wonderful 3D platformer, but I wouldn't call it a "collect-a-thon" as others seem apt to because there isn't
much to collect. It is basically a love-letter to Gamecube-era Nintendo; the game structure is like Mario 64/Sunshine and the art style is very Windwaker.
The overall story of A Hat in Time is simple: Hat Girl lost all her magical hourglass Time Pieces and she needs to explore and do missions to get them back. Getting them back opens up new worlds to do more missions, and eventually you fight the final boss. It's short, sweet, and (importantly) gets you into the action really fast. The only qualm I have with the overarching story is that it introduces the big villain early in a largely linear selection of missions, and forgets about them entirely until you're ready to fight them in the end.
Individual Chapter / Act (World / Level) themes are an incredibly strong point in this game. Each Chapter is unique and imaginative so you never know what's around the next corner. Starting in a very Mario Sunshine-esque island town, you move to another chapter where you complete meta goals to settle a dispute between two bird producers, anoter is a horror romp complete with a straight horror-game level, to a large sandbox level that almost completely abandons the Chapter / Act structure of the rest of the game. Each of these chapters is filled with top-notch humor that had me laughing out loud on many, many occasions as well. I highly recommend checking every interactable object you can.
Overall, the story, world, and humor are probably the game's strongest assets but the gameplay's no slouch either.
A Hat in Time is a shockingly solid platformer. Hat Girl has all sorts of tricks like running up walls, double jumps, dashes, and dives and it is a treat to control her. Extra care is put into a lot of little things, too: Hat Girl has a small hop when she lands from a jump, giving her a nice bouncy weight, and she's got a dedicated "make a :steammocking: face" and can blow kisses, to boot.
Control-wise I only have a few wishes that, while they don't break the great feeling, would've still been nice. I wish she at least had an animation for chaining jumps on the ground, they don't need to be a Mario-style triple jump or anything, but connecting jumps like that is always great. Otherwise, I don't really see a reason sliding to a stop in a dive means you cannot move until you hop out of it, it'd be nice if input on the stick caused her to auto-hop out of it. Neither of these things are deal-breakers and are very nitpicky, but I think they'd help more than they'd hurt.
The "Hat" part of A Hat in Time comes in the Hat system where, throughout the game, Hat Girl collects new hats that give her new powers while wearing
hat like simple sprinting, turning into a block of ice, and momentarily slowing down time. This is an incredibly cute theme, but breaks the breakneck pacing of the gameplay with the constant need to switch between them. In addition, some of the hats are so specific in their use that oftentimes the game needs to put in that hat's specific obstacle just to remind you that you have it. The Ice Hat is the chief offender here, where its obstacle is just a springboard that will launch Hat Girl a place she could otherwise not reach, no platforming involved, just a check to make sure you didn't somehow lose that hat.
Badges are another thing Hat Girl collects that give her varying passive powers, up to three different slots. These powers range from the entirely-non-optional hookshot that lets you grapple from grapple points, to other useful abilities like not colliding with and being knocked back by platforms if you jump-dive into them, to a magnet that attracts nearby pickups. This system suffers from a few issues similar to the hat system where, because you can change them anytime you want, it occasionally slows down gameplay just to have to put on one badge for a specific type of obstacle and then change back when you complete it. It's incredibly irritating that the grapple ability is a badge you basically have to always have equipped as well, if only because changing back and forth between it and another badge whenever you see a grapple point is so tedious.
A Hat in Time is, unsurprisingly, not without bugs. Most of these are small and handled well-enough in game. For example, if the engine doesn't ever know exactly what's happening after a jump, it simply returns Hat Girl to where she started it. This is definitely preferable to getting stuck, falling out of bounds, or crashing and I commend the simple way it was handled.
Other bugs are a little less graceful and there's one cannon in particular that can never seem to shoot me facing the right direction to then grapple from the intended grapple hook. It takes a bit of finnagling to try and get Hat Girl turned around so it works.
Otherwise, the game ran at a smooth 1080p60 with no noticeable hitches. I hear there are strange issues at ~144Hz when using a controller, but I am unable to confirm nor deny that as I only play at 60.
A Hat in Time is one of those games that had me questioning my cliched 5 star rating system. It's incredibly fun and I really enjoyed every minute of playing it, but it's definitely neither perfect or a genre redefining piece of innovation. In the end, though, I still consider it a great game, making it 5/5 Stars. If it where a 1-10 rating, however, it'd probably be a high 8 to 9.
Either way, I fully recommend A Hat in Time to anyone, it is truly a great game. Especially give it a look if you like 3D platformers, or things that are way too cute for this world.
